articles.title: HUMAN 3.0 – A Map To Reach The Top 1%
articles.description: 一套最大化个人潜能的全方位指南。
articles.english:
As corny as this may sound, I’ve always wanted to become a force to be reckoned with.

An absolute unit of an individual.

Not just having a nice and muscular body, but to be fully developed in every domain of life.

I wanted to become multidimensionally jacked. I wanted to max out all of my stats. I didn’t want to be an NPC. I wanted to be a level 100 player. All areas of the map unlocked. Maxed out physicality, intellect, and professions. Bank overflowing with gold. I wanted to do it all. Mind, body, spirit, relationships, money.

This desire has drastically influenced my life.

As a teenager, I became obsessed with fitness. Then, I wanted to absorb as much knowledge as possible. Then I wanted to be free, so I failed at various business models until I finally made one work. I’ve had various spiritual and philosophical stints that I believe have helped me see “superficial pursuits” like money and fitness in a completely different light than the average person.

Over the past 15 years, I’ve researched the depths of psychology, personal development, philosophy, social dynamics, technology, the internet, startups, money, religion, and meaning.

After writing about my findings online for the past 5 years, I’ve noticed critical overlapping patterns that have begun to form a new philosophy for today’s world.

That’s where HUMAN 3.0 comes in.

I want to synthesize everything I’ve learned into one comprehensive map to navigate the modern landscape. I want to provide you with the knowledge, skills, and principles that help you escape mediocrity and actualize your highest potential. I will attempt to make this as non-dogmatic and science-backed as possible, but I also want to get the point across with clarity and conviction. I plan to write this for today’s world using clear, natural language while simplifying these concepts as best I can so that this doesn’t turn into a forgotten textbook. For that reason, I am going to speak how I speak and pass the nuance off to you. The nuance and critical thinking always lie with the reader.

This will be an ongoing series where we dissect the human experience and reprogram your reality to live the best life possible.

Much of it will be wrong, and I encourage you to question what I say. In fact, I hope that you can build this out with me. If you talk about HUMAN 3.0 in your own writing or content, I’d love to see it. Take these ideas and build on them. If you like the H3.0 model, use it.

Now, there are plenty of incredible models and gurus already out there.

Spiral Dynamics (psychology), Buddhism & Christianity (meaning), Materialism and Mentalism (nature of reality), eCommerce & consulting (business), Red Pill & Feminism (social dynamics), and so on. Anywhere you look, you can find hundreds of models that promise you the answer to all your problems.

All have their truths, but the critical flaw is that they are all isolated to one domain of life. We learn math, English, and science as singular, siloed classes when knowledge is a web. We dissect frogs in a lab and draw conclusions without considering the entirety of the ecosystem and interconnected relationships from which they come. Beyond that, and for some this is hard to swallow, many spiritual teachers have frail bodies. Many businessmen can’t maintain relationships. Many “alpha males” are emotionally unaligned. While these are incredible accomplishments in their own regard, it is rare that one is truly self-developed.

Even if these models or gurus do connect multiple domains, like Ancient Greek philosophies, they were often prevalent before the internet, technology, and AI started to change everything. On a more important note, very few touch on areas such as work and money, which is surprising, as those dominate most people’s minds and lives.

Today, we will lay the foundation of HUMAN 3.0.

Over the coming months (maybe years), we will uncover what it truly means to live life to its fullest. I will not be able to cover all of the details that this model contains in this introduction.

HUMAN 3.0 – A Model To Maximize Your Potential

This model offers the big picture. It is not a dogmatic set of actionable steps, but a set of guidelines for reaching your maximum potential and bust through mental, physical, spiritual, and vocational plateaus faster. It orients patterns found across human development and builds on top of various scientific, psychological, spiritual, and vocational models that have already done a lot of the heavy lifting.

My goal is to take the best parts of the world’s greatest theories and apply them to the life of the individual.

Once you understand this model, you can begin to map where your current level of development lies within each quadrant (your Archetype) and what your overall development looks like (your Metatype). Then, you can attempt to move further toward a 3.0+ Level Metatype – one who has maximized all areas of life.

We will discuss those later in this letter, but for now, let’s understand the foundation.

1) Quadrants

The foundation of Human 3.0 is four quadrants that represent the four domains of life.

Mind (Personal Mental World) – Your thoughts, emotions, beliefs, and internal world. How you interpret the world.

Body (Personal Physical World) – Your behavior and physical appearance. How the world interprets you. Includes nutrition, training, hobbies, habits, grooming, communication, apparel, etc.

Spirit (Collective Mental World) – Your relationship to your environment, community, culture, family, friends, colleagues, and reality. How you derive meaning and connection.

Vocation (Collective Physical World) – Your relationship to systems, structures, and social institutions like education, career, and the economy. How you fit into and contribute to society.

Adapted from Ken Wilber’s AQAL model, the quadrants represent the four fundamental perspectives, creating a generalized map of all knowledge and experience.

This map of reality prevents partial thinking and doesn’t reduce problems to one perspective. An internal mental problem may not be best solved by vocational means like getting a new job. A spiritual problem may not be best solved by bodily means like nutrition. A capitalist and Christian are developed in their respective domains, but will experience unnecessary pain when trying to apply their model to problems within other domains. Money often doesn’t solve for meaning and vice versa, but that doesn’t mean they aren’t intimately connected. All of these domains overlap, and by developing yourself in all of the above you begin to live a life where you become in control of your future.

Since life, development, and evolution follow a general unfolding toward more chaos or complexity, and ordered structures are created to contain that chaos, we can call the process of life, especially your personal life, “problem solving.”

A seed unfolds until it becomes a flower. A flower is many times more complex than a seed, and to reach that state, it needs resources from its environment to self-develop. The seed has the natural desire to grow, and through many courses of evolution, it has solved the problems that have led to many other species of plants dying off.

One may not think the seed is consciously trying to grow or solve problems. Still, through observation and connecting patterns to our personal life, that’s what we would call it, since we have created language. We can start to understand that there is a natural flow of life toward greater complexity. Complexity introduces problems, and to constrain the entropy that stems from complexity, an ordered structure must emerge through creation.

In your own personal evolution, you have the desire to reach your potential → you take a step into the unknown and are introduced to complexity → you acquire knowledge and skill to solve problems that prevent forward movement (or stagnate and let chaos consume you) → your identity expands and ascends to a new level → the process repeats unless you get stuck.

This pattern can be noticed across all planes and domains of reality. I encourage you to think through more examples, but for the sake of brevity, let’s move on.

2) Levels

Within each quadrant, there are 3 macro levels of development that represent low consciousness (1.0), mid consciousness (2.0), and high consciousness (3.0).

These levels are adapted from various models in developmental psychology, such as Spiral Dynamics and the 9 Stages of Ego Development, which are already well-researched overlays of many psychological theories. In short, these have shown that our mind (our values, beliefs, and worldview that influence how we think and make decisions) evolves through predictable stages over time.

Human 1.0 (The Conformist) – Values established authority and traditions. Characterized by narrow-mindedness, black and white thinking, and believing there is only “one right way,” which often stems from childhood conditioning.

Human 2.0 (The Individualist) – Rejects the norm and pursues their own goals. Has the desire to acquire status and be perceived as valuable. They are less narrow-minded, but now believe that their way is the one right way.

Human 3.0 (The Synthesist) – Able to adopt multiple perspectives, connect various patterns of reality, and strategize new paths. They understand that all perspectives hold truths that can be synthesized for more holistic and mutually beneficial results. They can display what some may perceive as level 1 traits, such as narrow-mindedness, but it is an intentional choice to tune out noise.

In a model like Spiral Dynamics, the “spiral” describes how individuals shift focus throughout their development between self and other (like rejecting the community of religion and embracing individual atheism). In Human 3.0, this happens when one reaches a new level in a specific quadrant. Someone can become an Individualist in Mind, which may cause a shift in focus toward Spirit, where they are still at the Conformist stage and submit to authority.

The descriptions of each level take different shapes in each quadrant, like how a 3.0 Synthesist in the Vocation quadrant (Lower Right) can effectively leverage AI to pursue their life’s work, while a 1.0 Conformist believes AI is purely evil due to a lack of knowledge, skill, and experience.

In the Body quadrant (Upper Right), a low consciousness individual has no understanding of the nutrition they put in their body, leading to obesity and sloth, because they haven’t acquired the Traits to make better decisions, while a high consciousness individual understands how various nutrients interact with their body and can tweak their diet to help serve their goals.

These levels reflect your complexity of self in any given domain. The entire Human 3.0 graph represents you. The more complex you are (by cultivating perspective and expanding consciousness), the more interesting life becomes, because you can choose the challenges you wish to take on. Like a video game: Level 1 is similar to an NPC or non-player character running on a script, Level 2 is the main character choosing their storyline, and Level 3 is the programmer who can create new games that others also enjoy playing.

Note: Lower or higher levels are not “bad” or “good,” they are points along someone’s individual journey. A person who is “high consciousness” is not better, just more developed, and that development has it’s obvious perks.

You do not leave any given level. You transcend and include the one before it. You acquire a greater perspective that allows you to leverage the knowledge, skill, and tools that you acquired during the lower stages.

We will discuss more examples in depth below.

3) Phases

Within each level, there are 3 phases of development that one must go through to reach the next level. Phases represent vertical development, moving up a level or regressing back down.

There are 3 general patterns that we can observe when an individual goes through a profound change:

Dissonance (Phase 1) – Once an individual has “gotten their taste” of their current stage of life, and if they do not get numbed by narrow-mindedness and comfort, they will feel tired of where they are, but unsure of what kind of life comes next.

Uncertainty (Phase 2) – If that individual becomes aware enough of their distaste, they take an uncertain step into the unknown and open themselves up to new knowledge and skill.

Discovery (Phase 3) – Like navigating a map, they discover the education, tools, resources, and insights that allow them to reach the next level of development.

For terminology’s sake, we can map specific areas of one’s life by appending the phase they are in to the level they are in within a particular domain.

As an example, “Vocation 2.1” (Level 2, Phase 1) would represent the development of collective exterior consciousness (relationship to systems, structures, and social institutions). The “2” represents the Individualist level, and “.1” represents that they have almost exhausted that stage and must take an uncertain step toward level 3 to discover what lies in their next chapter. For the Vocation quadrant, this could mean that they have pursued a new career, but realized they were climbing the wrong ladder, and need to make a shift toward discovering their calling.

Individuals can easily experience False Transformation during this process. They may feel as if they’ve advanced through each phase to reach a new level, but they are simply imitating what that level of development would look like without the required trait development. This is self-deception and traps people in their current stage, preventing them from progressing further until they solve the remaining problems that exist at their current level.

This False Transformation can happen when one develops themself in one domain (like the domain of mind) and they assume they have advanced in another (like the domain of spirit or vocation).

Individuals can also regress to a lower level during a temporary period of stress or when a problem outside their current level comes into their life. This explains why you may look back to a time where “things felt better” and you yearn to bring that sensation back to the present.

An enjoyable life, as shown in flow psychology and the musings of many philosophers such as Nietzsche, resides in the progression through these phases by overcoming resistance. Profound change rarely happens by accident. When you are intentional about your vision, goals, and priorities without regressing by nature of distractions and comfort, the chaos that would consume most people during these phases becomes tolerable and often the most fulfilling parts of life that you hold close to your heart.

At level 3 and beyond, individuals can pursue more complex challenges and simulate these phases for the love of the game (like a CEO who sells their company, becomes depressed, and starts another one from a more enlightened point of view), and since they create the game, it becomes infinite.

4) Traits

Within each phase, there is a threshold of knowledge, experience, and skill that must be acquired before the next levelreveals itself to you. While phases represent vertical development, traits represent horizontal development, or navigating the unknown until you have discovered enough to reach the next phase.

Each quadrant, level, and phase presents different challenges that demand a certain level of skill. That skill requires experimentation and education.

One can be knowledgeable in fitness, but without practice and experience, they become the fat personal trainer archetype. Their knowledge is admirable, but few people take them seriously, which has it’s pros and cons.

The trap with both vertical (phases) and horizontal (traits) development is boredom and anxiety. If you attempt to jump to a new level of development without the skill and experience to do so, you will become anxious and fail. If you do not attempt to move up a level at all, you will grow bored and resort to comfort and distraction.

Both boredom and anxiety lead to disorder in the mind and remove you from the unfolding flow of evolution. Your life may seem okay, but everything feels dull and meaningless.

That leads us into Channels – a way to combat disorder and make substantial progress.

5) Channels

When you reach the Dissonance Phase of any Level, you gain the ability to leverage a “Channel.”

Think of a Channel as an exciting quest in a video game. A rabbit hole of knowledge or skill. When you can’t stop researching a topic or working on a project and time passes by surprisingly quick.

On the Human 3.0 Graph, you can see that one end of the Channel is in the knowledge Trait while the other is in the skill Trait. Usually, a person becomes “obsessed” with learning or building, and that results in rapid experience gain moving them quickly toward their next Level of development within a specific quadrant.

A few examples would be:

Mind – Becoming immersed in a deep meditative state (skill) or following a line of thought that keeps you up at night, resulting in a plethora of ideas that light up your brain (knowledge).

Body – You find a new diet, supplement, or methodology and binge watch all possible content you can about it (knowledge). You become obsessed with running or lifting for a 3 month period, making more gains than you ever have before (skill).

Spirit – Mystical experiences. Honeymoon phases. Intimate moments. Finding a philosophy that “clicks” with your current phase of life. And so on.

Vocation – Reaching a point of maximum clarity that quickly leads into an exciting career change, product launch, or creative stint (skill). You find the perfect opportunity and can’t stop learning the required skills to start a business (knowledge).

The process for entering a Channel is as follows.

First, you must reach the Dissonance phase after you fully acclimate to the Level you are in. Once you grow tired of where you are, and if you don’t become numb to your problems, you use your distaste as fuel to push into the unknown. You create an aim or vision or goal within a specific quadrant (like Body). You begin acquiring knowledge and skill. You learn and do. You make mistakes and refine your aim. You experiment enough until you find the Channel that you get sucked into.

You can tell someone is in a Channel by how excited they are when they talk about it, like someone who has reached the point of writing a book where the words can’t stop flowing. They have vision. Their skill and knowledge provide a sense of clarity that allows them to shoot forward in progress.

When you are in the Dissonance phase, the best advice I can give is to search for excitement and enthusiasm and pursue that without shame, because that shame signals a lower Level of Mind, and you can develop the skill of confidence during that process.

There are certain tactics to force yourself into a Channel that we will call “Glitches” – like a glitch in the matrix, if the matrix were the boundaries of Level 1 and 2 until you create your own in Level 3.

Psychedelics can force someone into a mystical experience. PEDs can accelerate fitness progress. Moving into an apartment you can’t afford can provide a real deadline, forcing you to learn and do until you make your side business work.

AI is the most recent and widely available Glitch that crosses into all domains. It can be used to self-develop or self-destruct rapidly. Taste and discerment is required. AI is only pure good or pure evil from a limited perspective.

Be careful with these, as while they accelerate progress, they can be incredibly high risk. For certain people with certain goals, they are smart. For most people, especially in Level 1, they are death sentences.

Max out your “natural” potential so you have ample experience and don’t get one-shotted. Knowledge and skill decrease risk.

If you feel lost, you are probably in a Dissonance phase, and if you stick it out, you can find your next Channel and fall back in love with life.

Archetypes & Metatypes

In future letters and videos, we can use the Human 3.0 Graph to understand people (like Jordan Peterson, Andrew Tate, or Alan Watts), or to overcome problems in your life, like not being able to make money or find a partner.

If you have a specific request for a problem you’re facing or a person you want to understand, reply to this letter.

In this model, I’ve included what are called Archetypes and Metatypes.

Archetypes – patterns of people that show up in specific quadrants and levels within those quadrants.

Metatypes – the synthesis of a single person’s four archetypes within each quadrant.

Think of Metatypes as a sort of personality test, but for one’s self-development.

I’ll create a list of Metatypes for a future letter and an AI prompt so you can find your Metatype.

In the example above, I am only showing 3 archetypes within each quadrant. There are many more than that, so please understand that these are not set in stone. I’m just having fun with these.

You’ll notice that there is a general progression from low consciousness to high consciousness as someone develops themself within a quadrant:

NPC → Player → Creator in the Mind quadrant describes someone who stops living by the script they were assigned at birth, starts playing their own game, then creates new games to play (similar to “construct-level” awareness).

Incel → Chad → Sigma or Beta Male → Alpha Male → Sigma Male in the Body quadrant are common archetypes we see in today’s world that you can observe in one’s behavior and appearance. This can correspond with other areas on the graph or have further causes within the same quadrant. Like how an Incel typically has higher estrogen levels from diet and environment, and how social structures in the Vocation quadrant have led to processed food and microplastics, which further exacerbate that problem on a mass scale.

Job → Career → Calling is one of many progressions in the Vocation quadrant. Relating to work, this can start with anything nowadays. Some people may not even have a job, or they go into their calling early in life. The key insight about the progression through each level is that they start with low consciousness (Conformist) and have the ability to progress to high consciousness (Synthesist).

Religion → Atheism → Mysticism in the Spirit quadrant is a common pattern (not the only pattern) that we see in those raised in a strict religious household, leading to rebellion. Then they rediscover a new perspective on God and loop back around to the truths that were contained in Level 1.

Ken Wilber’s “pre-trans fallacy” occurs when people confuse pre-rational (Conformist) states with trans-rational (Synthesist) states because both appear “non-rational” from a conventional rational (Individualist) perspective. This can happen both ways.

One can elevate a Level 1 primitive state to Level 3 status, and some often reduce genuine Level 3 development to being primitive thinking.

In other words, a “bible thumper” with lack of knowledge and experience beyond their childhood conditioning finds it difficult to take a mystic seriously, when the mystic often holds the same truths, but from a more comprehensive perspective.

If it helps, think of the IQ bell curve meme.

Of course, this is only one minor example of how developmental progression can play out in the Spirit quadrant. There are various patterns across personal relationships, sports, families, scientific or metaphysical beliefs, and more.

There are dozens to hundreds of archetypes within each quadrant, not just the three I displayed in each.

Now, for the example given above, when we plot points of development within each quadrant, level, phase, and trait, we gain a comprehensive understanding of where a certain individual lies. (You can see this in the opaque white shape on the map.)

This specific example of a person would be at Human 2.0.

How do we come to that?

For every point in Level 1, they receive 1 point.

For every point in Level 2, they receive 2.

For every point in Level 3, they receive 3.

Then, we can divide by the total amount by 12 (the total number of developmental slices on the graph), resulting in 2.0.

In this example, we can create a description for their development within each quadrant as follows:

Mind – No longer lives by a script and is close to construct level awareness.

Body – Ungroomed and has poor habits, but occasionally exudes confidence.

Spirit – Believes in the literal interpretation of God, but is tolerant of atheist friends and peers.

Vocation – Has a valuable set of education and skills, but is focused on a safe and fulfilling career.

If we were to map more than just 3 Archetypes per quadrant, this would become a lot more complex and comprehensive, but we will save that for future letters.

Now, if we take those descriptions and merge them into one, we get their Metatype. I plan to use AI for this because I don’t want things to be a static “personality test” that puts you in one of 16 generalized boxes.

In this case, we can consider this person’s Metatype to be “The Outlier.” In brief, this is someone who has drifted away from mainstream patterns without rebellion, operating from a countercultural lens. They don’t care about their appearance, but this may be False Transformation, as they lack experience in the Body quadrant.

This is only the foundation of the Human 3.0 model, so we have a lot more nuance to unpack.

– Dan
articles.chinese:
【文章标题】人类3.0——通往顶尖1%的路线图  
【这是第1/9部分】

尽管听上去可能有点老套，但我一直渴望成为一股不容小觑的力量。  

一个绝对意义上的“完整个体”。  

这不仅意味着拥有匀称健硕的体魄，更意味着在人生各个维度上都实现充分发展。  

我想成为一个“多维强化版”的人；我想把自身所有能力参数全部拉满。我不想当一个毫无自主意识的NPC（非玩家角色），而想成为等级100的顶级玩家——整张地图全部解锁，体能、智力与专业能力全部登峰造极，银行账户金币满溢。我想把一切做到极致：心智、身体、精神、人际关系、财富。  

这一渴望深刻地塑造了我的人生轨迹。  

少年时期，我痴迷于健身；随后，我渴望尽可能多地吸收知识；再后来，我追求自由，于是尝试过多种商业模式却屡屡失败，直至最终找到一条可行之路。我也曾经历不同阶段的灵性探索与哲学思辨，这些经历让我得以用一种迥异于常人的视角，重新审视金钱、健身等看似“浅层”的追求。  

过去十五年间，我深入钻研心理学、个人成长、哲学、社会动力学、科技、互联网、初创企业、财富、宗教与生命意义等领域。  

过去五年，我持续将研究成果在线分享，逐渐发现若干关键性的重叠模式——它们正悄然汇聚成一套契合当今时代的新哲学体系。  

“人类3.0”便由此诞生。  

我希望将迄今所学融会贯通，凝练为一张全面、实用的现代生存指南，助你驾驭当下纷繁复杂的现实世界。我愿为你提供切实可用的知识、技能与原则，助你挣脱平庸桎梏，真正活出自己最高的潜能。我会尽力让这套体系保持开放包容、立足科学实证；同时，也力求以清晰有力的语言直抵核心。我计划用今天这个时代最自然、最易懂的语言来书写，并尽最大努力化繁为简，避免它沦为一本被束之高阁的教科书。正因如此，我将采用自己惯常的表达方式，把细微之处与深层思辨交由你来把握——真正的思辨权与判断力，永远属于读者本人。  

这将是一场持续展开的系列探索：我们将共同解构人类经验，重新校准你的现实认知，从而活出此生最丰盛、最本真、最卓越的生命状态。  

其中许多观点难免有失偏颇，我诚挚邀请你质疑我所说的每一句话。事实上，我更希望你能与我一同构建、拓展它。如果你在自己的写作或内容创作中提及“人类3.0”，我很乐意拜读；欢迎拿走这些想法，加以延展、深化。如果你认同H3.0模型，请放心使用它。  

当然，当下已有大量极为出色的理论模型与意见领袖。  

例如：螺旋动力学（心理学）、佛教与基督教（关于生命意义）、唯物主义与唯心主义（关于实在本质）、电商与咨询业（商业实践）、“红药丸”思潮与女性主义（社会关系动力学），等等。无论你朝哪个方向望去，都能轻易找到数百种声称能一举解决你所有问题的模型。

【文章标题】人类3.0——通往顶尖1%的路线图  
【这是第2/9部分】

每种理论都有其合理之处，但关键缺陷在于：它们全都局限于生活的某一个领域。我们把数学、英语和科学当作彼此割裂、互不关联的单科来学习，而知识本应是一张相互交织的网络；我们在实验室里解剖青蛙，却在得出结论时全然不顾它所归属的整个生态系统，以及其中错综复杂的依存关系。更进一步说——对某些人而言，这一点或许难以接受——许多灵性导师身体孱弱；许多商人无法维系亲密关系；许多自诩为“阿尔法男性”的人情绪失衡、内在失调。尽管这些成就本身已属非凡，但真正实现全方位自我成长的人，实属凤毛麟角。

即便某些模型或导师（如古希腊哲学体系）确实尝试贯通多个领域，它们也大多成形于互联网、现代科技与人工智能彻底重塑世界格局之前。更重要的是，极少有理论深入探讨工作与金钱这类议题——这令人惊讶，因为这两者恰恰占据着绝大多数人思想与生活的中心位置。

今天，我们将为“人类3.0”奠定基础。

在接下来的数月（甚至数年）里，我们将共同探寻何谓真正充盈丰盛的人生。本次导论篇幅有限，我无法详尽展开这一模型所涵盖的所有细节。

人类3.0——一套最大化个人潜能的模型  

该模型提供的是全景式框架，而非一套教条式的具体操作步骤；它是一套指导原则，旨在助你更快突破心智、身体、精神与职业发展中的各类瓶颈。它梳理并整合了人类成长过程中反复出现的共性模式，并建立在大量既有成果之上——包括各门科学、心理学、灵性传统及职业发展理论，它们早已完成了大量基础性探索与实证工作。

我的目标，是萃取全球最卓越思想体系之精华，并将其切实应用于个体生命实践之中。

一旦你理解了这一模型，便可开始定位自己当前在每个象限中的发展水平（即你的“原型”），并勾勒出自身整体发展的全貌（即你的“元型”）。继而，你可努力向“3.0+级元型”迈进——那是一种在人生所有维度上均已臻至高度成熟与平衡的理想状态。

这些概念我们将在后文详述，但此刻，让我们先夯实根基。

1）四大象限  

“人类3.0”的根基由四大象限构成，分别对应人生的四个基本领域：

心智（个人心智世界）——你的思维、情绪、信念及内在世界；你如何诠释外部世界。

身体（个人物质世界）——你的行为表现与外在形象；外部世界如何感知你。涵盖营养、锻炼、兴趣爱好、日常习惯、仪容仪表、沟通方式、着装风格等。

精神（集体心智世界）——你与所处环境、社群、文化、家庭、朋友、同事乃至现实本身的关系；你如何从中获得意义感与联结感。

志业（集体物质世界）——你与各类系统、结构及社会制度的关系，例如教育体系、职业路径与经济生态；你如何融入社会并为之作出贡献。

【这是第3/9部分】

该模型改编自肯·威尔伯（Ken Wilber）的AQAL模型，其中四个象限代表四种根本性的观察视角，由此构成一幅涵盖全部知识与经验的通用地图。

这幅现实地图可防止片面思维，避免将问题简单归结为单一视角。例如，一个内在的心理问题，未必能通过职业手段（如换一份新工作）获得最佳解决；一个灵性层面的问题，也未必能靠身体层面的方式（如调整营养）来妥善应对。一位资本家和一位基督徒，各自在其所属领域内都已充分发展，但若试图将自身那套认知模式生搬硬套到其他领域的问题上，则难免遭遇不必要的痛苦。金钱往往无法赋予生命以意义，反之亦然；但这并不意味着二者彼此割裂——事实上，它们紧密相连。所有这些领域彼此交叠；而当你在上述所有维度上持续成长，便开始真正掌握自己未来的主动权。

由于生命、发展与演化总体遵循一种朝向更高无序性或复杂性的展开趋势，而有序结构正是为了容纳这种无序性而被创造出来，因此我们可将生命过程——尤其是你个人的生命历程——称为“解决问题”。

一颗种子不断展开，最终绽放为一朵花。花朵远比种子复杂得多；要抵达这一状态，它必须从环境中汲取资源，实现自我发育。种子天生具有生长的倾向，而经由漫长的演化历程，它已成功解决了诸多难题——正因如此，许多其他植物物种才在演化中走向消亡。

或许有人会认为，种子并非有意识地努力生长或解决问题。然而，通过观察，并将其中呈现的规律与我们自身的生命体验相联结，我们便会如此定义它——毕竟，人类创造了语言。由此我们开始理解：生命天然趋向于日益复杂的展开；而复杂性本身又会带来新的问题；为约束由复杂性所引发的熵增，唯有通过创造，方能催生出新的有序结构。

在你个人的演化进程中，你怀有实现潜能的渴望→你迈出一步，踏入未知之境，随之迎来复杂性的挑战→你获取知识与技能，用以解决阻碍前行（或导致停滞不前，任由混乱吞噬自我）的各种问题→你的身份认同随之拓展、跃升至全新层次→这一过程循环往复，除非你中途陷入停滞。

这一模式在现实的所有层面与领域中皆清晰可见。我鼓励你自行思考更多实例，但为行文简洁起见，我们暂且继续往下推进。

2）层级  

每个象限内部，均包含三个宏观的发展层级，分别对应低阶意识（1.0）、中阶意识（2.0）与高阶意识（3.0）。  

这些层级借鉴自发展心理学中的多种成熟模型，例如螺旋动力学（Spiral Dynamics）与自我发展的九阶段理论（9 Stages of Ego Development）。这些模型本身已是大量心理学理论经过深入研究后所形成的整合框架。简言之，已有充分证据表明：我们的头脑（即塑造我们思维方式与决策逻辑的价值观、信念与世界观）会随时间推移，经历一系列可预测的阶段性演化。

人类1.0（顺从者）——崇尚既定权威与传统。其特征是思维狭隘、非黑即白，笃信世上只存在“唯一正确的方式”，这种信念往往源于童年时期所受的条件化影响。

人类2.0（个体主义者）——拒绝随波逐流，执着追求个人目标。渴望获取社会地位，并希望被他人视为有价值之人。他们虽不再那么狭隘，却转而坚信“自己的方式才是唯一正确的方式”。

人类3.0（整合者）——能够采纳多重视角，联结现实中的各类模式，并据此规划全新路径。他们深知每一种视角都蕴含部分真理，而将这些真理加以整合，便能达成更全面、更具互惠性的成果。他们有时会展现出某些可能被他人视为“1.0层级”的特质（例如思维狭隘），但这实为一种主动选择——为屏蔽干扰噪音而刻意为之。

在螺旋动力学（Spiral Dynamics）这类模型中，“螺旋”一词描述的是个体在成长过程中，其关注焦点如何在“自我”与“他人”之间不断转换（例如，先否定宗教社群，继而拥抱个人化的无神论）。在人类3.0阶段，这种转变发生于个体在某一特定象限中达到新层次之时。例如，某人在“心智”象限（上左）已成长为个体主义者，这可能导致其关注焦点转向“精神”象限（上右），而在此象限中，他仍处于顺从者阶段，继续服从权威。

每个层级在不同象限中的具体表现形态各不相同：例如，在“职业”象限（下右），一位3.0层级的整合者可高效运用人工智能来推进毕生志业；而一位1.0层级的顺从者则因缺乏知识、技能与经验，断然认定人工智能纯粹邪恶。

在“身体”象限（上右），意识水平较低的个体对自身摄入的营养毫无认知，因而陷入肥胖与怠惰——因为他们尚未习得支撑更优决策所需的各项特质；而意识水平较高的个体则清楚各类营养素如何与自身身体相互作用，并能灵活调整饮食，以切实服务于自身目标。

这些层级反映的是你在任一特定领域中自我的复杂程度。整张人类3.0图谱即是你自身的映射。你越复杂（通过培养多元视角、拓展意识疆域而实现），人生便越富趣味，因为你得以自主选择想要迎接的挑战。这恰如电子游戏：1级玩家类似按脚本运行的NPC（非玩家角色）；2级玩家则是主角，可自行选择剧情走向；3级玩家则升格为程序员，不仅能创造新游戏，还能让其他玩家乐在其中。

注意：层级的高低本身并无“好坏”之分，它们仅标志着个体独特成长旅程中的不同坐标点。“高意识水平”者并非更优越，只是发展得更为成熟；而这种成熟自然带来显而易见的优势。

你并不会真正“离开”某个层级，而是超越它并涵纳它——你获得一种更宏阔的视角，从而得以调用此前各低阶阶段所积累的知识、技能与工具。

3）阶段

在每一层级内部，个体需经历三个发展阶段，方能跃升至更高层级。这些阶段体现的是纵向发展——即向上跃迁或向下倒退。

当个体经历深刻转变时，我们可观察到三种普遍模式：

失谐（第一阶段）——一旦个体已“尝过”当下人生阶段的滋味，且未因狭隘与安逸而变得麻木，便会对自己所处的状态感到疲惫，却又不确定接下来的人生该走向何方。

不确定性（第二阶段）——倘若个体对这种不适感有了足够清醒的认知，便会怀着犹疑迈出一步，踏入未知领域，并向新的知识与技能敞开自我。

发现（第三阶段）——如同依图导航，他们逐步发掘出通向下一发展阶段所需的教育路径、实用工具、可用资源及关键洞见。

为便于术语统一，我们可在特定生活领域中，将个体当前所处的层级与其所处的阶段相结合，以标识其具体发展状态。

举例而言，“职业2.1”（第二层级，第一阶段）代表集体外在意识的发展（即个体与系统、结构及社会制度的关系）。其中“2”指代“个体主义”层级，而“.1”则表明个体已几乎耗尽该层级的发展潜力，必须鼓起勇气、迈入未知，朝第三层级迈出不确定的一步，从而探明人生下一章的真意。就“职业”这一象限而言，这可能意味着：个体曾尝试转行，却最终意识到自己正攀爬的是一架错误的梯子，因而亟需转向，去探寻真正属于自己的志业。

在此过程中，个体极易陷入“虚假转化”。他们可能自以为已顺利历经各阶段、成功跃升至新层级，实则只是在模仿该层级应有的外在表现，却并未完成相应内在特质的实质性成长。这是一种自我欺骗，会将人牢牢困于当前层级，使其无法继续前行，直至彻底解决当前层级所存在的根本问题。

这种“虚假转化”往往发生于：个体仅在某一领域（如心智领域）实现了自我提升，便误以为自己在另一领域（如灵性领域或职业领域）也同步取得了进展。

此外，个体也可能在遭遇短期压力，或生活中突然出现超出其当前层级所能应对的问题时，暂时倒退回较低层级。这也解释了为何你有时会回望过去，觉得“那时一切更美好”，并渴望将那种感受重新带回当下。

正如心流心理学及尼采等众多哲学家的思索所揭示的那样，一种令人愉悦的人生，正蕴藏于主动跨越这些阶段、不断克服阻力的过程之中。深刻的转变极少偶然发生。当你对自己的愿景、目标与优先事项保持高度自觉，不因外界干扰或安逸诱惑而倒退时，那些本会令大多数人深陷混乱的阶段，反而变得可以承受，甚至成为你内心最珍视、最具满足感的生命体验。

在第三层级及更高层级上，个体便能主动迎接更复杂的挑战，并出于对“游戏”本身的热爱而模拟这些阶段（例如一位CEO卖掉公司后陷入抑郁，继而以更通透的视角重新创业）。由于他们自身即是这场游戏的创造者，游戏便由此变得无限延展。

4）特质  

在每个阶段内部，都存在一道门槛：唯有积累起特定程度的知识、经验与技能，下一阶段才会向你显现。如果说阶段代表的是纵向成长，那么特质则体现为横向拓展——即在未知领域中持续探索，直至所获足以支撑你迈入下一阶段。

每个象限、每个层级、每个阶段，均呈现不同的挑战，而应对这些挑战，又需匹配相应的能力水平；这种能力，唯有通过实践尝试与系统学习方能获得。

一个人或许精通健身知识，但若缺乏实际训练与亲身经验，就极易沦为“肥胖的私人教练”这类典型反差形象。其知识固然令人钦佩，却鲜有人真正信服——这本身亦有其利弊。

纵向发展（阶段）与横向发展（特质）共同面临的陷阱，是厌倦与焦虑。倘若尚未具备相应技能与经验，便贸然跃升至新层级，你将陷入焦虑并最终失败；反之，若完全拒绝向上突破，则会日渐乏味，转而沉溺于安逸与分心。

厌倦与焦虑二者皆会导致心智失序，使你脱离生命自然演进的流畅节奏。你的生活表面看似无虞，实则一切皆显黯淡、空洞而毫无意义。

这便引出了“通道”——一种对抗失序、实现实质性进步的有效路径。

5）通道  

当你抵达任一层次的“不谐阶段”时，便获得了调用一条“通道”的能力。

不妨将“通道”想象成电子游戏中一段激动人心的冒险任务：一个知识或技能的“兔子洞”。当你对某个主题的研究或某个项目的投入达到欲罢不能的程度，时间便悄然飞逝，浑然不觉。

在《人类3.0图谱》中可见，一条通道的一端连结着“知识”特质，另一端则连结着“技能”特质。通常，人们会因痴迷于学习或创造而全情投入，从而在特定象限内快速积累经验，迅疾迈向下一个发展层级。

若干实例包括：  

心智层面——沉浸于深度冥想状态（技能），或执着于某条思辨线索，辗转反侧至深夜，脑中迸发出大量灵感火花（知识）。

身体层面——你发现了一种新饮食法、新型营养补充剂或某种新方法，便如饥似渴地狂看所有你能找到的相关内容（知识）；你连续三个月痴迷于跑步或力量训练，取得的进步远超以往任何阶段（技能）。

精神层面——神秘体验、热恋期、亲密时刻、觅得一种与当下人生阶段“完美契合”的哲学观，等等。

职业层面——抵达一种极致清晰的状态，随即迅速开启令人振奋的职业转型、产品发布或创意爆发期（技能）；你邂逅了天赐良机，因而无法停止学习创业所需的一切技能（知识）。

进入“通道”（Channel）的过程如下：

首先，你必须在完全适应当前所处层级后，进入“不谐期”（Dissonance）。一旦你对现状感到厌倦，且并未对自身问题变得麻木，便可将这份不适转化为动力，勇敢踏入未知领域。你在某一特定象限（例如“身体”）内确立一个目标、愿景或志向；继而开始积累知识与技能：边学边做，边犯错边校准方向；不断尝试，直至找到那个令你深深沉浸、欲罢不能的“通道”。

判断某人是否已进入“通道”，只需观察他谈及此事时的兴奋程度——那就像一位作家写到酣畅淋漓之际，文字奔涌而出、不可遏止；他目光坚定，知识与技能共同赋予他一种澄澈的明晰感，使其得以在进步之路上疾驰向前。

当你身处“不谐期”时，我能给出的最佳建议是：主动追寻内心的兴奋与热忱，并毫无羞怯地投入其中——因为那份羞怯恰恰暴露了你仍处于较低层级的心智状态；而恰恰是在这一过程中，你能够锤炼出真正的自信。

还有一些策略可强行将自己推入“通道”，我们称之为“故障点”（Glitches）——如同《黑客帝国》中矩阵的系统漏洞；只不过此处的“矩阵”，指的是第一、二层级所设下的认知边界，直到你在第三层级亲手构建起属于自己的新秩序。

致幻剂可强行触发神秘体验；性能增强药物（PEDs）能加速体能进步；搬进一间你负担不起的公寓，则会带来真实紧迫的截止期限，迫使你拼命学习、全力行动，直至副业真正运转起来。

人工智能（AI）则是最新近、也最普及的“故障点”，它横跨所有领域。它既能助人飞速自我成长，亦能令人顷刻自我瓦解。能否善用，端赖品味与判断力。从狭隘视角出发，才会断言AI纯粹是善或纯粹是恶。

请慎用这些“故障点”：它们虽能加速进展，却也蕴含极高风险。对某些人、在某些目标下，它们不失为明智之选；但对大多数人——尤其是尚处第一层级者而言，它们无异于死刑判决。

务必先竭尽所能开发自身的“自然潜能”，积累足够丰富的实践经验，以免被一击击垮。知识与技能，正是降低风险的根本保障。

倘若你感到迷茫，很可能正身处“不谐期”；只要坚持下去，终将觅得下一个“通道”，重新爱上生活。

原型与元类型

【这是第8/9部分】

在今后的信件与视频中，我们可以借助“人类3.0图谱”来理解各类人物（例如乔丹·彼得森、安德鲁·泰特或艾伦·瓦茨），也可用它来应对你生活中遇到的实际难题，比如难以赚取收入，或迟迟无法找到人生伴侣。

如果你正面临某个具体问题，或希望深入理解某个人，请直接回复这封信。

在此模型中，我纳入了所谓“原型”（Archetypes）与“元类型”（Metatypes）两类概念。

原型——指在图谱各象限及其内部不同层级中反复出现的人格模式。

元类型——则是一个人于四个象限中各自所呈现的原型之综合体现。

可将元类型视作一种面向自我成长的人格测评工具。

我将在后续信件中列出常见元类型清单，并配套提供一个AI提示词（prompt），助你精准识别自己的元类型。

上文示例中，每个象限仅展示了三种原型；实际上原型远不止这些，因此请务必明白：这些分类并非一成不变，目前仅为趣味性探索。

你会注意到，在任一象限内，个体的自我发展往往呈现出一条从低意识水平向高意识水平演进的普遍路径：

心智象限中的“NPC → 玩家 → 创造者”，描述的是这样一类人：起初按出生时被赋予的既定脚本生活；继而开始主动“玩自己的游戏”；最终更进一步，创造出全新的游戏规则（类似“建构层次”层面的觉知）。

身体象限中的“非自愿独身者（Incel）→ 查德（Chad）→ 贝塔男/西格玛男 → 阿尔法男 → 西格玛男”，是当今社会中常见的一组原型，可从人的行为举止与外在形象中直观观察到。它们可能与其他象限的状态相互关联，也可能源于同一象限内的深层成因。例如，“非自愿独身者”体内雌激素水平偏高，常与其饮食结构及生活环境相关；而职业象限中的社会结构问题（如工业化食品体系与微塑料污染），又在宏观层面上加剧了这一生理失衡。

职业象限中，“工作 → 职业 → 召唤”是众多发展路径之一。就工作而言，如今起点可以是任何状态：有人甚至尚未就业，也有人早在青年时期便已步入自己的“召唤”。这一演进路径的关键洞见在于：每一层级均始于低意识状态（顺从者），并具备向高意识状态（整合者）跃升的潜能。

精神象限中，“宗教信仰 → 无神论 → 神秘主义”是一条常见（但非唯一）的发展轨迹，多见于严格宗教家庭出身者：先经历反叛式疏离，继而以全新视角重新体认神性，最终回归第一层级中原本蕴含的真理。

肯·威尔伯提出的“前—超谬误”（pre-trans fallacy），指人们常将前理性阶段（顺从者）与超理性阶段（整合者）混为一谈——因为在常规理性阶段（个体主义者）看来，二者皆显得“非理性”。这种混淆可能双向发生：一方面，有人将第一层级的原始状态错误拔高至第三层级；另一方面，也有人将真正成熟的第三层级发展，轻率贬低为原始思维。

【文章标题】人类3.0——通往顶尖1%的路线图  
【这是第9/9部分】

换言之，一位仅囿于童年教养、缺乏更广博知识与阅历的“圣经鼓吹者”，往往难以认真对待一位神秘主义者——尽管后者所持守的真理与其并无二致，却拥有更为宏阔、整全的视角。

若有助于理解，不妨想想那个关于智商分布的钟形曲线梗图。

当然，这仅是精神（Spirit）象限中发展进程展开方式的一个微小例证。类似模式还广泛存在于人际关系、体育运动、家庭互动、科学或形而上学信念等各个领域。

每个象限内部都蕴含着数十乃至上百种原型，远不止我在各象限中所展示的三种。

回到上述例子：当我们把个体在每个象限、每个层级、每个阶段及每项特质上的发展程度逐一标定后，便能全面把握此人所处的整体发展位置。（地图上那个不透明的白色形状即为此人发展坐标的可视化呈现。）

本例中这位人士的发展定位，即为“人类2.0”。

我们是如何得出这一结论的呢？

——在第一层级（Level 1）的每一项指标上，计1分；  
——在第二层级（Level 2）的每一项指标上，计2分；  
——在第三层级（Level 3）的每一项指标上，计3分。  

随后，将总分除以12（即图表中全部发展切片的总数），结果即为2.0。

据此，我们可对这位人士在各象限中的发展状况作如下描述：

心智（Mind）——不再机械遵循既定脚本，已接近建构主义层面的觉知水平；  
身体（Body）——疏于打理，日常习惯欠佳，但偶尔流露出自信气质；  
精神（Spirit）——信奉对“上帝”的字面化解读，却能包容无神论的朋友与同侪；  
志业（Vocation）——具备扎实的教育背景与实用技能，但职业选择倾向安稳且富意义的方向。

倘若我们在每个象限中纳入的原型远不止三个，整个模型将变得更为复杂，也更为周全；不过这部分内容，留待后续通信再详述。

现在，若将上述四方面描述整合为一，便得到此人的“元类型”（Metatype）。我计划借助人工智能来完成此项整合工作，因为我不希望它沦为一种静态的“人格测试”，将人粗略归入十六种泛化标签之一。

就本例而言，此人的元类型可界定为“异类者”（The Outlier）。简言之，这是一种悄然偏离主流轨迹、却并不刻意反抗的人；其思维视角天然带有反文化色彩。他们毫不在意自身外在形象，但这种状态或许属于“虚假转化”——因其在身体（Body）象限中尚缺乏切实历练。

以上，仅是“人类3.0”模型的基石；后续尚有大量精微之处有待深入剖析。

——丹

sentences.english: As corny as this may sound, I’ve always wanted to become a force to be reckoned with.
sentences.chinese: 尽管听起来有点老套，但我一直渴望成为一个不容小觑的力量。

sentences.english: I wanted to become multidimensionally jacked. I wanted to max out all of my stats.
sentences.chinese: 我想成为一个多维度‘练满’的人——把所有能力值都拉到顶点。

sentences.english: I didn’t want to be an NPC. I wanted to be a level 100 player.
sentences.chinese: 我不想当一个非玩家角色（NPC），而想成为等级100的主角。

sentences.english: This desire has drastically influenced my life.
sentences.chinese: 这种渴望深刻地塑造了我的人生。

sentences.english: As a teenager, I became obsessed with fitness.
sentences.chinese: 青少年时期，我对健身达到了痴迷的程度。

sentences.english: Then, I wanted to absorb as much knowledge as possible.
sentences.chinese: 之后，我渴望尽可能多地吸收知识。

sentences.english: I’ve had various spiritual and philosophical stints that helped me see 'superficial pursuits' like money and fitness in a completely different light.
sentences.chinese: 我经历过多种灵性与哲学探索，这让我对金钱、健身等所谓‘表层追求’有了截然不同的认知。

sentences.english: Over the past 15 years, I’ve researched the depths of psychology, personal development, philosophy, social dynamics, technology, and meaning.
sentences.chinese: 过去15年里，我深入研究了心理学、个人成长、哲学、社会动力学、科技与生命意义等领域。

sentences.english: After writing about my findings online for the past 5 years, I’ve noticed critical overlapping patterns.
sentences.chinese: 过去五年在线分享我的发现后，我注意到了一些关键的共通模式。

sentences.english: I want to synthesize everything I’ve learned into one comprehensive map to navigate the modern landscape.
sentences.chinese: 我想将所学全部整合成一张全面的地图，助你驾驭当代世界。

sentences.english: I will attempt to make this as non-dogmatic and science-backed as possible, but I also want to get the point across with clarity and conviction.
sentences.chinese: 我会尽力让这套模型既避免教条化，又具备科学依据；同时以清晰有力的方式传达核心观点。

sentences.english: For that reason, I am going to speak how I speak and pass the nuance off to you.
sentences.chinese: 正因如此，我将用自己真实的语言表达，并把细微之处的解读权交还给你。

sentences.english: The nuance and critical thinking always lie with the reader.
sentences.chinese: 对细节的把握与批判性思考，永远属于读者本人。

sentences.english: Much of it will be wrong, and I encourage you to question what I say.
sentences.chinese: 其中很多内容可能是错的，我鼓励你质疑我所说的每一句话。

sentences.english: We dissect frogs in a lab and draw conclusions without considering the entirety of the ecosystem.
sentences.chinese: 我们在实验室解剖青蛙，却忽视了整个生态系统及其相互关联。

sentences.english: It is rare that one is truly self-developed.
sentences.chinese: 真正实现全方位自我发展的人，实属罕见。

sentences.english: Even if these models or gurus do connect multiple domains, they were often prevalent before the internet, technology, and AI started to change everything.
sentences.chinese: 即便某些模型或导师试图打通多个领域，它们大多诞生于互联网、科技与人工智能彻底重塑世界之前。

sentences.english: This model offers the big picture. It is not a dogmatic set of actionable steps, but a set of guidelines for reaching your maximum potential.
sentences.chinese: 该模型提供宏观图景——它并非一套教条式的行动步骤，而是一组助力你实现潜能上限的指导原则。

sentences.english: Once you understand this model, you can begin to map where your current level of development lies within each quadrant (your Archetype) and what your overall development looks like (your Metatype).
sentences.chinese: 一旦理解该模型，你就能定位自己在每个象限的发展阶段（即你的‘原型’），并勾勒出整体发展轮廓（即你的‘元类型’）。

sentences.english: Mind (Personal Mental World) – Your thoughts, emotions, beliefs, and internal world. How you interpret the world.
sentences.chinese: 心智（个人心理世界）——你的思想、情绪、信念与内在世界，即你如何诠释外部世界。

sentences.english: Body (Personal Physical World) – Your behavior and physical appearance. How the world interprets you.
sentences.chinese: 身体（个人物理世界）——你的行为与外在形象，即世界如何解读你。

sentences.english: Spirit (Collective Mental World) – Your relationship to your environment, community, culture, and reality. How you derive meaning and connection.
sentences.chinese: 灵性（集体心理世界）——你与环境、社群、文化及现实的关系，即你如何获得意义感与联结感。

sentences.english: Vocation (Collective Physical World) – Your relationship to systems, structures, and social institutions like education, career, and the economy.
sentences.chinese: 志业（集体物理世界）——你与教育、职业、经济等系统、结构及社会制度的关系。

sentences.english: An internal mental problem may not be best solved by vocational means like getting a new job.
sentences.chinese: 内在的心理问题，未必能通过换工作这类职业手段得到最佳解决。

sentences.english: A seed unfolds until it becomes a flower. A flower is many times more complex than a seed.
sentences.chinese: 种子不断展开，终成花朵；而花朵的复杂性远超种子本身。

sentences.english: You have the desire to reach your potential → you take a step into the unknown → you acquire knowledge and skill → your identity expands → the process repeats.
sentences.chinese: 你渴望实现潜能 → 迈入未知领域 → 获取知识与技能 → 自我认同随之拓展 → 此过程循环往复。

sentences.english: Human 1.0 (The Conformist) – Values established authority and traditions. Characterized by narrow-mindedness and black-and-white thinking.
sentences.chinese: 人类1.0（顺从者）——崇尚既有权威与传统，思维狭隘、非黑即白。

sentences.english: Human 2.0 (The Individualist) – Rejects the norm and pursues their own goals. Has the desire to acquire status and be perceived as valuable.
sentences.chinese: 人类2.0（个体主义者）——拒绝常规，追求个人目标，渴望获得地位并被视作有价值之人。

sentences.english: Human 3.0 (The Synthesist) – Able to adopt multiple perspectives, connect various patterns of reality, and strategize new paths.
sentences.chinese: 人类3.0（整合者）——能采纳多元视角，联结现实中的各种模式，并规划全新路径。

sentences.english: You do not leave any given level. You transcend and include the one before it.
sentences.chinese: 你不会抛弃任一既有层级，而是超越并涵纳前一层级。

sentences.english: Dissonance (Phase 1) – Once an individual has 'gotten their taste' of their current stage, they will feel tired of where they are, but unsure of what comes next.
sentences.chinese: 失谐期（第一阶段）——当一个人已充分体验当前阶段后，会感到厌倦现状，却又不知未来方向。

sentences.english: Uncertainty (Phase 2) – They take an uncertain step into the unknown and open themselves up to new knowledge and skill.
sentences.chinese: 不确定期（第二阶段）——他们怀着犹疑迈入未知，主动向新知识与新技能敞开自我。

sentences.english: Discovery (Phase 3) – They discover the education, tools, resources, and insights that allow them to reach the next level.
sentences.chinese: 发现期（第三阶段）——他们找到教育路径、实用工具、可用资源与深层洞见，从而跃升至下一发展阶段。

sentences.english: False Transformation can happen when one develops themself in one domain and assumes they have advanced in another.
sentences.chinese: 虚假转化可能发生在：某人在某一领域有所成长，却误以为自己在另一领域也同步进阶。

sentences.english: An enjoyable life resides in the progression through these phases by overcoming resistance.
sentences.chinese: 充实的人生，蕴藏于穿越这些阶段并克服阻力的过程之中。

sentences.english: Think of a Channel as an exciting quest in a video game — a rabbit hole of knowledge or skill.
sentences.chinese: 可将‘通道’想象成电子游戏里激动人心的任务——一个让你深陷其中的知识或技能盲区。

sentences.english: When you are in the Dissonance phase, search for excitement and enthusiasm and pursue that without shame.
sentences.chinese: 当你处于失谐期时，请追寻兴奋感与热情，并毫无羞耻地投入其中。

sentences.english: AI is the most recent and widely available Glitch that crosses into all domains.
sentences.chinese: 人工智能是最新、最普及的‘系统漏洞’，它能穿透所有发展领域。

sentences.english: If you feel lost, you are probably in a Dissonance phase, and if you stick it out, you can find your next Channel and fall back in love with life.
sentences.chinese: 若你感到迷茫，很可能正身处失谐期；只要坚持下去，便能找到下一条‘通道’，重新爱上生活。

sentences.english: Metatypes – the synthesis of a single person’s four archetypes within each quadrant.
sentences.chinese: 元类型——一个人在四个象限中各自原型的综合体现。

articles.title: Self-discipline is easy, actually
articles.description: 重新定义自律，解释为何明确的目标比盲目用力更有效。
articles.english:
If you have to force yourself to do it, you will lose.

That’s what most people get wrong about discipline. They hear that word… discipline… and a montage of grueling workouts with David Goggins running and screaming starts playing in their mind. They think they need to lash themselves to do the work that leads to something good in their life.

“The pain of discipline must outweigh the pain of laziness” has a lot of truth to it, as does struggle being the part of a story worth telling, but most successful people didn’t hate the entire journey. In fact, it was fun to them. They wanted to do the hard thing. And that points to a massive insight:

You are already disciplined toward the exact goals you are supposed to be.

That’s how the mind works.

> Goals are conditioned into your mind by your environment

> Your goals become your filter for reality, shaping what you focus on and what you forget

> Your brain helps you notice and remember information that helps achieve those goals

> Naturally, you act toward those goals and your identity solidifies

Discipline is a feature of identity

Someone who deeply identifies as a good student (after an entire childhood of their parents telling them they should pursue that goal) doesn’t have to force themselves to study for 12 hours a day. It’s just who they are.

A bodybuilder who went through a breakup and was tired of having low self-confidence doesn’t struggle to eat healthy or show up to the gym every day. In fact, it is painful if they don’t. Because if they don’t, they aren’t any closer to their goal, and since that goal is so intertwined with who they are, they feel as if their survival is at stake, because it is. Humans survive on both the physical and conceptual level (genetics and memetics, we feel threatened if something important to us is threatened, no matter if it’s our pet dog or pet belief).

This is where it gets interesting.

A gamer doesn’t have to force themselves to stare at the computer and perform for multiple hours at a time. Someone who loves a TV show will lie down and binge-watch the entire series. Someone who procrastinates their work – because that goal doesn’t align with them – will endlessly scroll their phone because their goal is to not achieve their goal.

These people aren’t “lazy,” they’re arguably self-disciplined, just toward a goal that results in immediate reward. That’s what discipline is, no? Persistent effort toward a goal. And boy is the average person persistent toward a mediocre life. Yes, most people are simply unconscious of the fact that their desire for comfort outweighs their desire for change. It is, in fact, their goal.

“But Dan! Those are easy and comfortable! They don’t take effort to do!”

Sure, and writing every day is comfortable for me. It’s more painful for me not to go to the gym than it is to go to the gym. I try to play video games like I did when I was younger and I just can’t. They’re boring and overstimulating. I have better things to do.

Human behavior is teleological. Cybernetic. The mind is a goal-achieving machine. We interpret the world with our identity as the lens, and the goals conditioned into our minds shape the behavior that forges who we are.

If we can understand this process, or reverse engineer it, we can leverage it to achieve nearly impossible goals.

You’re reading this because you are trying to force yourself to be disciplined. But that will never work. Whether you’re trying to make more money or study for your exams, if you follow this process, you won’t have to worry about distractions or procrastination.

Limbo is the laboratory

The reason you want to be disciplined is that you’ve exhausted your current stage of life.

You’re starting to notice that you’ve stalled out.

You’re starting to notice that every day is the same as the last.

You’re starting to notice that if you keep doing the same things, you won’t achieve the life you want.

You’re in limbo, and you don’t want to be there anymore.

It’s painful. But you misinterpret that pain and think of the first solution that comes to mind: be more disciplined. This is where most people get stuck in a loop of forcing themselves to do something they don’t want to do, just to quit two weeks later and go back to the life they swore against.

Pain is the signal that change is happening.

The way out is to lean in. To become aware of how painful your current life is. Because once the pain of where you are outweighs the pain of where you want to be, discipline is no longer painful, because you don’t have to force yourself to do it.

Step one is to write out:

Everything you hate about your current life (I don’t want to hear about positive thinking right now, you’re wrong).

Exactly what kind of life you will have if you don’t change those things.

Then, sit with it for a week. Contemplate it. Go on a walk and let your mind dance with those ideas. After some time, and if you don’t hide from the pain, you will start the next chapter of your life.

If that doesn’t work, there’s a bit more we can do.

Discipline isn’t built, it’s discovered

I’ve been training in the gym for about 12 years now.

I’ve been writing every day for about 5.

I’ve walked 10k steps every day for about 4.

For all of the above, the first time I tried to form the habit, I fell off multiple times. I remember being invited on a walk and thinking it was for senile old people. I was confirming the thoughts that helped me achieve the goal of staying the same. I didn’t want to do those things but felt like I had to. When I finally formed the habit, it was different than the other times I when I tried to force it. They weren’t “hard” to do. They were the byproduct of experimentation and discovery.

All of those habits became a part of my life for 3 specific reasons:

I was deeply aware of a painful problem in my life

I searched for evidence to support a desirable future version of myself

I changed my physical and digital environments to solidify my new identity

I blocked out time during the week to do those things as if I were going to be doing them for the rest of my life

In middle school, my self-confidence was abysmal. I was extremely tall and lanky. I felt awkward in my own skin, so I wanted to change that. I used that pain as motivation to educate myself on fitness and nutrition. I even remember reading “Nutrient Timing For Peak Performance” on my bus rides to school. I started doing push-ups in my room, started going to after-school weights, and my love for the gym picked up from there.

To change my environment, every day after I got home from school, I would go straight to the computer and watch 2-3 of my favorite fitness vloggers on YouTube. They’d give me programs, exercises, and diet tips to try. They were my role models as a teenager, and they shaped most of what I do today. Don’t neglect the positive power of social media.

This entire time, I didn’t pick a random diet or training routine while forcing myself to stick with it because someone told me it was good to do. The common theme with people who are dissatisfied with their life is that they allow the confident advice of others to shape the majority of it.

I treated this as a period of discovery and experimentation.

I was collecting vision. I was test-driving pieces of my future self.

I read the nutrition book because it sounded interesting. I couldn’t help but be curious. It could solve my problem. As I read it, I wanted to try certain novel tactics I was learning, like eating 50g of simple carbs and 25g of protein before exercise like some Olympic athletes do. (This is how I read most books by the way. I don’t force myself to read anything, and I don’t read consistently. I read books that I can’t help but read, and I’m okay with going long periods without reading a thing.)

As I watched fitness vlogs, I found new exercises to try, and I was always excited to try them. This wasn’t difficult. It didn’t require force. It was fun to try things that could change my life. With time, all of the little things I learned morphed into a deep understanding of fitness and nutrition.

I became my own teacher and trainer.

The problem here is that (1) most people aren’t hyper aware of a painful problem in their life, so their mind doesn’t release dopamine at the sight of a potential solution and (2) they learn without experimentation, so they never make the progress necessary to act as a feedback loop that keeps them motivated.

How to engineer an identity

Step one is recognition. Who you are determines what you consider important. You must first recognize that you are pursuing a series of goals whether you are conscious of them or not. Those goals frame how you interpret reality, and you usually notice things that confirm your current way of life.

The goals your mind operates on stem from conditioning, and conditioning stems from your environment. Your parents, teachers, and culture have put you on a path that is heading toward a dead end.

Step two is strategic dissonance. To avoid getting trapped in a state of feeling lost – limbo – you let the divide between who you are and who you want to be grow wider. You cultivate dissatisfaction with your current lifestyle by noticing where you will end up if you don’t change.

By becoming aware of the problems in your life, you prime your mind for pattern recognition. Your brain starts to confirm that change is the right thing to do and helps you notice the information that can aid in that.

Step three is environment engineering. Unfollow people who don’t put out information that helps you achieve a better life. Throw away the food that you allow yourself to eat at 3am. Pull out a paper and map out exactly what you are going to do that week down to the hour. Review and iterate every week. You need that feedback loop.

Immerse yourself in the people, places, and things that provide you with things to try. Follow new accounts even if you disagree with them. Scroll through Amazon until you find a book that sounds interesting, even if you only end up reading the first few pages. Intention is what matters. Intention is you giving a direction for your mind to rewire itself toward.

Step four is self-experimentation. Because problems that aren’t solved through experimentation aren’t solved for good. Rather than being assigned another goal, you try everything until you find the one thing that you can’t pull yourself away from. Then, you repeat that process until it becomes who you are.

Thank you for reading.

– Dan

【文章标题】自律其实很简单  
【这是第 1/4 部分】

如果你必须强迫自己去做一件事，那你终将失败。

这正是大多数人对“自律”最大的误解。一听到“自律”这个词，他们脑海中立刻浮现出大卫·戈金斯（David Goggins）一边狂奔、一边嘶吼的严酷训练画面。他们以为，唯有用鞭子抽打自己，才能完成那些通向人生美好结果的工作。

“自律之痛，必须压倒懒惰之痛”这句话确有其道理；同样，奋斗本身也确实是值得讲述的故事中不可或缺的部分。但事实上，大多数成功者并非憎恨整段旅程——恰恰相反，他们乐在其中。他们真心渴望去做那些艰难之事。而这揭示了一个极为关键的洞见：

你早已对本该追求的目标展现出高度的自律。

这正是人类心智的运作方式。

> 你的目标由所处环境潜移默化地塑造进你的意识之中  
> 这些目标进而成为你感知现实的滤镜，决定你关注什么、遗忘什么  
> 你的大脑会主动帮你留意并记住一切有助于实现这些目标的信息  
> 于是，你自然而然地朝这些目标行动，而你的身份认同也随之日益稳固  

自律，是身份认同的一种自然表征。

一个从小被父母反复告知“你应当成为优秀学生”的人，若已将“好学生”这一身份深植于心，便无需强迫自己每天苦读十二小时——那不过是“他本来的样子”。

一位因分手而长期缺乏自信的健美运动员，并不会为坚持健康饮食或每日准时去健身房而挣扎。相反，若他不去做这些事，反而会感到痛苦。因为一旦停步，他就离目标更远一步；而这个目标早已与他的自我认同密不可分——以至于他本能地感到生存受到威胁。的确如此：人类既依靠生理层面（基因）存活，也依靠观念层面（模因）存续；当对我们至关重要的事物——无论是宠物狗，还是珍视的信念——受到威胁时，我们都会本能地感到危险。

事情到这里才真正变得有趣起来。

一名游戏玩家无需强迫自己紧盯屏幕、连续数小时投入操作；一个痴迷某部电视剧的人，会心甘情愿地躺下，一口气刷完整季；而一个总把工作一拖再拖的人——只因那个目标与他毫不契合——则会无休止地刷手机，因为他真正的目标，恰恰是“不达成那个目标”。

这些人并非“懒惰”，恰恰相反，他们甚至堪称高度自律——只是自律的方向，指向的是能带来即时回报的目标罢了。而这，不正是自律的本质吗？——即持续不懈地朝某个目标付出努力。天哪，普通人对平庸人生的执着，可真够持久的！没错，多数人只是未曾察觉：自己对安逸的渴望，早已悄然压倒了对改变的渴求。而这份对安逸的向往，本身就是他们的目标。

“但丹！这些事轻松又舒服啊！根本不需要费力去做！”

当然如此。每天写作对我来说也很轻松；不去健身房，反而比去健身房更让我难受。我试着像年轻时那样打电子游戏，却怎么也提不起劲——它们既无聊又过度刺激。我还有更有意义的事要做。

【文章标题】自律其实很简单  
【这是第 2/4 部分】

人类行为具有目的性，也具有控制论特征。心智本质上是一台目标实现机器。我们透过“自我身份”这副透镜来理解世界，而内化于心智中的目标，则塑造着我们的行为，并最终铸就我们成为怎样的人。

倘若我们能理解这一过程，甚至逆向拆解它，便能借力于它，去达成那些看似遥不可及的目标。

你正在阅读这段文字，正因为你正试图强迫自己变得自律。但这条路注定走不通。无论你是为了赚更多钱，还是为了备考复习，只要遵循接下来介绍的这套方法，你就再不必为分心或拖延而忧心忡忡。

“ limbo”（悬而未决之境）就是你的实验室  

你渴望自律，是因为你已耗尽了当下人生阶段的所有可能性。  
你开始意识到，自己已然停滞不前；  
你开始察觉，日复一日，生活千篇一律；  
你开始明白：若继续沿袭旧有模式，你终将无法活成自己真正想要的样子。  
你正身处一种悬而未决的状态，而你已厌倦于此。

这种状态令人痛苦。但你误解了这份痛苦，下意识地认定：只要更自律，问题就能解决。这恰恰是多数人陷入恶性循环的起点——强逼自己去做并不真心想做的事，结果两周后便彻底放弃，重新退回那个曾发誓要逃离的生活里。

痛苦，其实是变化正在发生的信号。  
出路在于迎难而上，在于清醒地体察当下生活有多令人煎熬。因为一旦“现状之痛”压倒了“改变之痛”，自律便不再是一种折磨——你不再需要强迫自己，它会自然发生。

第一步，请如实写下：  
你当前生活中所有令你厌恶之处（此刻请别跟我谈什么积极思维，你错了）；  
倘若你对这些现状不作任何改变，未来你将过上怎样一种生活。

然后，静心与这份清单共处一周。反复思量它；出门散个步，任思绪自由徜徉、与这些念头共舞。只要你没有逃避那份痛感，经过一段时间的沉淀，你的人生自会开启崭新的篇章。

倘若这一步仍未能奏效，我们还有更深一层的方法可循。

自律并非“打造”而成，而是“发现”所得  

我已在健身房训练约12年；  
坚持每日写作约5年；  
每天步行一万步约4年。  

以上所有习惯，最初尝试建立时，我都曾多次半途而废。我还记得，当初有人邀我一起散步，我竟觉得那是给老糊涂的老人准备的活动。那时，我正不断强化那些助我维持现状的念头——我并不想做这些事，却总觉得“不得不做”。而当我最终真正养成习惯时，体验与以往截然不同：它不再是我咬牙硬撑的结果。这些行动本身并不“艰难”，而是探索与发现过程中的自然产物。

所有这些习惯之所以能融入我的生命，源于三个具体原因：  
一、我对自身生活中某个切肤之痛有着深刻而清醒的认知；  
二、我主动搜寻证据，以支撑那个理想中、更值得期许的“未来的我”。

【文章标题】自律其实很简单  
【这是第 3/4 部分】

我调整了自己的物理环境与数字环境，以巩固全新的自我认同。

我每周都预留出固定时间来做这些事，仿佛自己将终其一生坚持下去。

中学时期，我的自信心低得可怜。我个子极高、身材瘦长，总觉得自己浑身不自在，因此迫切想改变现状。我将这份不适感转化为动力，主动学习健身与营养知识。至今仍记得，上学路上乘公交车时，我常捧着《巅峰表现的营养时机》这本书阅读。我在房间里开始做俯卧撑，放学后去参加力量训练课程，从此爱上了健身房。

为重塑所处环境，每天放学回家后，我都会立刻坐到电脑前，在YouTube上观看两到三位我最喜爱的健身博主发布的视频。他们为我提供训练计划、动作指导和饮食建议。青少年时期的他们，是我心目中的榜样，也塑造了我今日绝大多数的习惯与选择。切勿忽视社交媒体所蕴含的积极力量。

在此期间，我从未随意挑选某种流行饮食法或训练方案，再强迫自己硬撑着坚持下去——仅仅因为别人说“这对你有好处”。那些对生活感到不满的人，往往有一个共性：任由他人自信满满的建议，主导自己人生的大部分走向。

我把这段时光视作一场探索与实验之旅。

我是在收集“愿景”，是在试驾未来那个“我”的各个组成部分。

我读那本营养学书籍，是因为它听起来很有趣；我无法抑制自己的好奇心，因为它或许真能解决我的问题。阅读过程中，我跃跃欲试书中介绍的新方法，比如像某些奥运选手那样，在运动前摄入50克简单碳水化合物和25克蛋白质。（顺便一提，我读大多数书都是这样：从不强迫自己读任何内容，也不追求持续阅读；只读那些让我欲罢不能的书，而长时间不碰一本书，我也完全不在意。）

观看健身视频时，我又不断发现新动作，总是满怀期待地去尝试。这并不费力，也无需强求；尝试那些可能彻底改变我人生的事，本身就是一件乐事。久而久之，我学到的点滴知识逐渐融会贯通，最终沉淀为对健身与营养的深刻理解。

我成了自己的老师，也成了自己的教练。

问题在于：（1）多数人并未高度警觉地意识到生活中某个真切的痛点，因此当看到潜在解决方案时，大脑并不会释放多巴胺；（2）他们仅靠被动学习，缺乏亲身实践，因而永远无法取得足以形成正向反馈的切实进步——而这种反馈，恰恰是维系长期动力的关键。

如何构建一种身份认同  

第一步是觉察。你是谁，决定了你认为什么重要。你必须首先意识到：无论是否自觉，你都在追逐一系列目标。这些目标框定了你理解现实的方式，而你通常只会注意到那些印证当下生活方式的信息。

【文章标题】自律其实很简单  
【这是第 4/4 部分】

你大脑所依循的目标，源于后天习得的条件反射；而这种条件反射，又源自你所处的环境。你的父母、老师和文化，早已将你推上了一条通往死胡同的道路。

第二步是“战略性失谐”。为避免陷入迷茫——即悬而未决的停滞状态——你要主动拉大“当下的你”与“你想成为的你”之间的差距。通过清醒地意识到：若不改变，自己终将走向何方，从而培养出对当前生活方式的不满。

当你开始觉察生活中存在的问题，你的大脑便被悄然激活，进入模式识别状态。它会不断印证：改变才是正确的选择，并主动帮你留意那些有助于实现改变的信息。

第三步是“环境重构”。取关那些无法为你提供更好生活所需信息的人；扔掉那些你凌晨三点还允许自己塞进嘴里的食物；拿出一张纸，精确规划出本周每小时要做的事；每周复盘并持续优化——你必须建立这样的反馈闭环。

让自己沉浸于能提供新尝试机会的人、场所与事物之中。即使观点相左，也主动关注新的账号；在亚马逊上随意浏览，直到发现一本听起来有趣的书——哪怕最终只读了前几页也无妨。关键在于那份意图：它正是你在为自己的大脑指明方向，引导它重新布线、自我重塑。

第四步是自我实验。因为唯有通过实验解决的问题，才能真正得到解决。你不再被动接受他人设定的目标，而是遍尝百法，直至找到那一件让你欲罢不能的事；然后反复投入其中，直到它内化为你自身的一部分。

感谢阅读。  

——丹

articles.title: You have about 36 months to make it
articles.description: 探讨当前时代背景下的致富竞赛与机会窗口。
articles.english:
I’ve been seeing this statement circulate online:

“You have about 36 months to make it.”

And it makes sense: AI is and will continue to replace jobs no matter how much people fight against it. Money as we know it will change or even cease to exist because millions of ASIs (artificial superintelligences) will rapidly execute tasks beyond human comprehension, dictating humanity’s future (see: AI 2027). Aside the point, this is the last time you’ll see absurd gains in cryptocurrency because the technology is being adopted and regulated. After it’s adopted, it becomes like stocks.

My intention with this letter isn’t to scare you or sound sensationalist. All of this is prediction and speculation. It can absolutely be wrong, and I expect most of it to be. I am simply setting the scene of the discussion happening in niche pockets of the internet. My hope is to provide you with a non-dogmatic perspective that allows you to notice opportunities and make decisions that don’t leave you trapped, because it is obvious that something is changing, and the future will come intensely fast.

I do not think you have 36 months to make it.

Instead, I think you have 36 months before the definition of “making it” is radically transformed.

Thankfully, human nature remains the same, and I can’t help but think that this period of rapid growth is marking a clear distinction between machines and humans.

Those who lean into their humanity will thrive.

Those who can’t stop identifying with mechanical living, on the other hand, will not.

Doers vs directors

We’re going to see 10 person $1B companies pretty soon… In a group chat I have with my tech CEO friends, there’s a betting pool for the first year that there will be a one-person $1B company.

– Sam Altman

One thing is certain:

The amount of power an individual has today is vastly more than any other moment in the past, and that will only continue to increase. This power transfer has occurred in 3 layers.

The internet gave people access to any and all knowledge. Power transferred away from schools and institutions.

Social media gave people the leverage to attract their own audience. Power transferred away from employers, publishers, centralized media, and even record labels. People can now learn, build, and earn without being dependent on someone else’s authority.

Artificial intelligence is giving people the ability to create, automate, and outsource almost anything. Power is transferring away from traditional gatekeepers and intermediaries. People will soon be able to operate at the level of large teams with a fraction of the manpower.

In short, you now have three superpowers to take control of your future.

Learning – the ability to adapt and figure out what actions you must take to get a specific result.

Persuasion – the ability to build trust and attract people to a mutually beneficial vision or narrative.

Execution – the ability to turn ideas into reality through automation, creation, and delegation.

This creates a clear distinction between those who will thrive and those who won’t.

Doers vs directors. Employees vs entrepreneurs. Low-agency vs high-agency. Those who assign work rather than having work assigned to them. Those who pursue their interests and do many things. Those who don’t need permission to solve a problem, and since new problems emerge as reality gets complex, and AI is accelerating complexity toward infinity, problems are infinite, therefore value in the form of solutions are infinite. Money, not as the US dollar but as value exchange, is also, in fact, infinite.

Those who prepare themselves to solve the problems of the future, even when nobody can possibly know what those problems can be, will win. Plain and simple. The One-Person Business Launchpad helps with this.

Taste is the new intelligence

The anti-AI crowd will lose.

There will be an uproar of highly emotional people attempting to discredit those who attempt to leverage AI in their work, especially their creative work. Ignore these people and do not become one, because maintaining a pessimistic mindset for the next few years will only lead to a destructive confirmation bias. You become what you focus on, and by focusing on trying to stop an avalanche from the bottom of the mountain, you will get crushed.

What these people don’t yet understand is that the way we create is evolving just before. Photography and video are extremely recent developments on the timescale of humanity. Photo editing software and computer-generated graphics allowed us to create such unrealistic scenes with a few button clicks. Yes, it’s difficult to create those things, but it is a lot easier than a few years ago. Just because a few clicks on your screen are being replaced with natural language doesn’t mean it’s any easier to create something we see as art, especially when what we see as art changes as culture does, and culture is shifting rapidly right now. We don’t consider people artists for what specific tool they use. We consider people artists for why and how they use the tool. We grade them on the final product. The story. The emotion. The vision. The soul. Not the hours of labor that went into creating it. You can spend 10 years or 10 seconds writing a book and call yourself an author, but that doesn’t mean the book is good.

This is what the anti-AI crowd gets wrong.

They lump anyone using AI into the same category. They see AI as a chat box for short sentences where you type “write this newsletter for me” or “generate this image for me,” and while the output of those requests may look visually appealing, that doesn’t mean they are art. It simply exposes that most people have put too much emphasis on the labor that goes into creating something visually appealing, so that it has become their identity, and people will fight tooth and nail to avoid limiting themselves less. I do not believe that art should be tied to the buttons of a tool people press, but to why they pressed that specific series of buttons.

I think we can all agree that outsourcing all thought and control to the AI won’t get you anywhere, but people who focus on this do not understand anything beyond the surface of what AI is. They don’t see that AI has become a programming language for language itself. They don’t see that you can give highly specific instructions to the AI to the point of having full control over the output (this is what most employed “creative work” is anyway, you’re executing project instructions that you didn’t set – this isn’t art but industrial work disguised under the job title of “artist”).

They don’t understand that a word is the new brush stroke, the new low-pass filter, the new select and mask. They don’t understand that every minor decision an artist makes that imbues their personal touch into their work is still available, and that they can create more than what their wildest dreams allowed without spending hours doing so, but they just can’t see beyond random text box generations.

The single distinction that will separate art from slop is taste.

In other words, nothing has changed. People just hate what’s new, and that new is shining a light on what mattered in the first place. If you can’t create art with AI, you were never an artist to begin with. You were simply good at using a tool. Tools get replaced.

Utility vs meaning

Silicon solves utility so carbon can transcend to meaning.

We hate long lines at the DMV. We hate when a server gets our order wrong. We hate meetings that could have been a 5-bullet point email. AI and automation solve necessary work that humans hate. On the other hand, we crave the potential for failure. We love the final batter in the 9th inning. We travel across the world for a 5 star dining experience. We cry at a wedding as the bride and groom read handwritten vows.

Machines are for speed, repetition, and necessity.

Humans are for story, novelty, myth and meaning.

Most people identify with the traits of a machine – the schooling, the job, the mundane tasks – and that’s exactly why general fulfillment is abysmal. There will be a lot of turbulence in this change, and those who haven’t mastered their mind won’t be happy with that, but we’ve collectively hated industrial living for decades now. You have no room to complain, because there’s a 99% chance that your life will be inconceivably better than it is today.

Zoom in and it’s scary, zoom out and it’s wonderful.

As mechanical work gets replaced, what’s left is meaning.

To figure out what you want in life, choose something you deeply care about, dissect it ruthlessly, and shamelessly share your story, values, vision, and accompanying life’s work in public to form an artisan-esque lifestyle with a small tribe of people who support what you do. Pair that with AI and you free up room for leisure: the ultimate compliment to creative work.

How to prepare

36 months to make it.

That’s not set in stone, but it’s as accurate a number as you’re going to get.

You can either sit back and do what you’ve been doing or use this as a moment of urgency to turn your life around. Personally, I don’t see why you wouldn’t pick the second option. Changing your life and setting yourself up for an incredible future doesn’t require you to drop everything and move across the country. It requires you to choose your work. It requires you to think. It requires you to pursue something you care about. It requires you to take risks, create a story worth telling, and share it with those who can benefit.

Everything that created “the good life” in the past is becoming a requirement.

1) Become a philosopher-builder

There are 2 types of people we tend to respect in today’s world.

Programmers vs marketers. Big picture vs technical details. Spiritual vs practical. Philosophers vs scientists.

The future demands that we merge these polar ends. A builder has always needed a thinker. A programmer not paired with a marketer almost always leads to a disappointing number of users. A hippy stuck in the sky and a scientist stuck in an atom are both missing the truth. Those who can embody this duality become unstoppable, and we’re already seeing it happen.

Job titles are merging from “designer” and “engineer” to “design engineer.” The tools, AI-powered or not, are at a point where people can do more without added hours of labor.

Creators are founding and fueling companies. Coders are generating millions of views on social media.

The peak of human ability lies in being a specialized generalist. Not so specialized that you get replaced in an instant or taken advantage of because you are identified with a credential, but not so generalized that you are effective at effectively nothing.

2) Become a filter for ideas

Ideas now matter more than execution.

If taste is the new intelligence, and curation is the new IQ test in a world where information is overflowing and anyone can create anything, choosing what ideas deserve to be executed deserves the first seat at the table.

Your mind must become a finely tuned signal-to-noise filter.

For that to happen, you must understand that your mind interprets reality based on your identity and worldview. Your values and beliefs. The code you live by. Your level of development. The vision you are attempting to actualize. Your brain releases dopamine when information is useful toward your main and overarching goals.

Since most people don’t have goals, or their goals were assigned by schools and jobs, this is an incredibly painful process, and only those who commit to a revolt against the default path in life will begin to tune their instinct in such a way that allows future-forward ideas to be caught and leveraged.

The only way to know what ideas are worth executing is to forge your own philosophy in the fire of trial and error.

3) Become an AI orchestrator

The first and foundational decision to make when adopting AI lies in when to leverage it and when to do it by hand.

Usually, that decision lies in what you enjoy doing. For me, that’s writing. While I have various prompts I use for research and developing ideas (one of my favorites is a prompt that takes the topic I give it and asks observational questions until I personally reach an “aha” moment I can use in my writing), all of my letters are written by hand. AI is a tool that enhances my writing rather than replacing it.

Outside of your craft, I see AI prompts as highly specialized employees. I hate marketing, so I train the AI on information from marketers I respect, give it my frameworks, examples, or sources of inspiration, and have it spit out a first draft that I can then refine according to instinct and taste. By the end, it is higher quality, but not much different than what I would have put out if I did it myself.

Specialize in your craft, orchestrate a fleet of tasteful prompts that align with your values and vision.

If you haven’t already started, the best way to learn AI is to try automating yourself out of a job.

Yes, that increases the chances of your current job being replaced, but you would have been replaced anyway if you could automate it, and at least this would upskill you to the point of either getting a promotion or being able to work for yourself.

I’ll continue digging into these in future letters.

Thank you for reading this one.

– Dan
articles.chinese:
【文章标题】你大约有36个月的时间来“成功”

【这是第 1/5 部分】

我最近在网上频频看到这样一句话：

“你大约还有36个月的时间来‘成功’。”

这话不无道理：人工智能正在并将继续取代工作岗位，无论人们如何抵制都难以阻挡。我们所熟知的“金钱”形态将发生改变，甚至可能彻底消失——因为数以百万计的人工超级智能（ASI）将以前所未有的速度执行远超人类理解能力的任务，从而主导人类的未来（参见《AI 2027》）。顺带一提，加密货币将迎来最后一次荒诞式暴涨，因为这项技术正迅速被主流采纳并纳入监管；一旦完成普及与规范，它就会变得和股票一样寻常。

我写这封信，并非要吓唬你，也无意制造耸人听闻的效果。以上所有内容，皆属预测与推测，完全可能出错，而且我预期其中大部分终将被证明是错误的。我所做的，只是为你勾勒出当下互联网某些小众圈层中正在展开的一场讨论图景。我的愿望，是为你提供一种不带教条色彩的视角，助你敏锐捕捉转瞬即逝的机遇，做出不致令你深陷困局的决策——毕竟，变革已然发生，而未来将以惊人的速度扑面而来。

我认为，你并非只有36个月来“成功”。

恰恰相反，我认为，你拥有36个月的时间，去适应“成功”这一概念本身即将发生的根本性重塑。

值得庆幸的是，人性始终如一。我不禁想到，这场迅猛发展的浪潮，恰恰清晰地划出了机器与人类之间的分野。

那些主动拥抱自身人性特质的人，将蓬勃生长；

而那些无法摆脱机械式生存状态、始终将自我等同于效率与流程的人，则注定步履维艰。

行动者 vs 决策者

很快，我们将见证仅由10人组成的公司估值突破10亿美元……在我与几位科技公司CEO朋友的群聊中，大家甚至已下注打赌：最早出现单人运营、估值达10亿美元的公司会出现在哪一年。

——萨姆·阿尔特曼

有一点毋庸置疑：

今天，个体所拥有的力量，远超人类历史上的任何时刻，且这种力量还将持续增强。这场权力转移，已通过三个层面悄然完成。

首先，互联网赋予每个人获取一切知识的权限，权力由此从学校与各类机构手中转移出来；

其次，社交媒体赋予个人吸引自有受众的杠杆，权力进一步从雇主、出版商、中心化媒体乃至唱片公司手中剥离——人们如今完全可以自主学习、自主创造、自主盈利，而无需依附于任何权威；

第三，人工智能正赋予个人近乎无限的创造、自动化与外包能力，权力正加速脱离传统守门人与中间环节。不久之后，一个人凭借极小的团队规模，便能实现过去需要庞大团队才能完成的产出。

简言之，你此刻已手握三项“超能力”，足以真正掌控自己的未来：

学习力——即持续适应、精准识别为达成特定目标所必需采取行动的能力；

说服力——即建立信任、凝聚人心，共同奔赴一个互利共赢的愿景或叙事的能力；

执行力——即借助自动化、创造与委托，将构想切实转化为现实的能力。

【文章标题】你大约有36个月的时间来实现突破  
【这是第2/5部分】

这清晰地区分了两类人：一类将蓬勃发展，另一类则不会。

行动者 vs 指导者；雇员 vs 创业者；低主动性者 vs 高主动性者；主动分配任务而非被动接受任务的人；主动追寻自身兴趣、广泛涉猎并付诸实践的人；无需他人许可便能着手解决问题的人。而随着现实日趋复杂，新问题层出不穷，人工智能又正以指数级速度加剧这种复杂性——直至趋于无限，问题本身也因此变得无穷无尽；相应地，以解决方案形式呈现的价值，同样无穷无尽。金钱——若不单指美元，而是泛指价值交换——事实上也同样是无限的。

那些主动为未来的问题做准备的人，即便无人能确切预知这些问题究竟为何，终将胜出。道理就是这么简单直接。“一人企业启动平台”正为此提供助力。

品味，即新时代的智力

反AI阵营必将落败。

届时将涌现大量情绪激烈的人，竭力诋毁那些试图在工作中（尤其是创意工作中）善用AI的人。请无视这类声音，更切勿沦为其中一员——因为在未来数年里持续抱持悲观心态，只会导致破坏性的确认偏误。你关注什么，就会成为什么；倘若只顾站在山脚徒劳地试图阻挡雪崩，最终只会被彻底掩埋。

这些人尚未意识到的是：人类的创作方式，其实正经历一场前所未有的深刻演进。摄影与视频，在人类历史长河中不过是极其晚近的产物。照片编辑软件与计算机生成图像技术，已让我们仅凭几次点击，就能创造出极度超现实的场景。诚然，创作此类作品依然不易，但相比数年前，已轻松太多。仅仅因为屏幕上的几次点击，正被自然语言指令所取代，并不意味着“艺术创作”本身变得更容易了——尤其当“何为艺术”的标准随文化变迁而不断流变，而当今文化正以前所未有的速度剧烈重塑。我们从不因某人使用何种工具而认定其为艺术家；我们判断一个人是否是艺术家，依据的是他为何使用这一工具、又如何使用它。我们评判的标准，是最终的作品：故事、情感、远见与灵魂，而非创作过程中耗费的工时。你可以花十年或十秒钟写一本书，并自称作家，但这并不意味着这本书就一定优秀。

这，正是反AI阵营的根本谬误所在。

【文章标题】你大约有36个月的时间来实现突破  
【这是第3/5部分】

他们把所有使用AI的人一概而论。在他们眼中，AI不过是一个用于输入简短句子的聊天框——比如“帮我写这期通讯”或“为我生成这张图片”。尽管这些请求的输出可能视觉上颇具吸引力，但这并不意味着它们就是艺术。它仅仅暴露出：大多数人过于强调创造出视觉吸引力所需付出的劳动，以至于这种劳动本身已成了他们的身份标签；人们会拼尽全力、寸步不让，只为避免自我设限。

我坚信，艺术不应与人们按下的工具按钮挂钩，而应取决于他们为何按下那一连串特定的按钮。

我想我们都能认同一点：若将全部思考与控制权悉数外包给AI，你终将一事无成。但那些只盯着这一点的人，其实对AI的理解仅停留在表面，从未深入其本质。他们看不到，AI已然演变为一种针对语言本身的编程语言；他们看不到，你完全可以向AI下达高度精准的指令，从而实现对输出结果的完全掌控（事实上，绝大多数受雇从事的“创意工作”本就如此：你只是执行他人设定的项目指令——这并非艺术，而是披着“艺术家”头衔外衣的工业化生产）。

他们不理解，“一个词”已等同于新的笔触、新的低通滤镜、新的选区与蒙版；他们不理解，艺术家在创作中所作的每一个细微抉择——那些赋予作品个人印记的瞬间——依然完全由自己掌握；他们更不理解，借助AI，创作者能实现远超昔日最狂野想象的成果，且无需耗费数小时苦熬；可他们偏偏只看得见随机文本框里蹦出的零散结果。

真正区分艺术与粗制滥造的唯一标尺，是品位。

换言之，一切从未改变。人们只是本能地排斥新事物，而这一次，新事物恰恰照亮了最初真正重要的东西。倘若你无法用AI创作出艺术，那你从一开始便不是艺术家——你只是擅长使用某种工具罢了。而工具，终将被取代。

效用 vs 意义  

硅基负责解决效用问题，以便碳基生命得以超越效用，抵达意义之境。  

我们厌恶车管所排起的长队；我们厌恶餐厅服务员弄错订单；我们厌恶那些本可用五条要点邮件就讲清却硬要开的会议。AI与自动化，正是为了解决人类深恶痛绝的必要性劳作。另一方面，我们却渴望失败的可能性：我们为第九局最后一击屏息凝神；我们跨越半个地球，只为赴一场五星餐厅的盛宴；我们在婚礼上热泪盈眶，只因新人正朗读亲手写就的誓词。  

机器，生来为速度、重复与必需而存在；  
人类，则为故事、新奇、神话与意义而存在。

【文章标题】你大约有36个月的时间来实现转变  
【这是第4/5部分】

大多数人将自我认同锚定在“机器”的特质上——接受学校教育、从事某份工作、日复一日完成琐碎任务——而这恰恰正是普遍性满足感极度匮乏的根源。这场变革必将伴随剧烈动荡，而那些尚未掌握自身心智的人，对此绝难感到满意；但事实上，我们早已集体厌倦工业化生活方式数十年之久。你根本没有资格抱怨，因为你的生活有99%的概率将变得比今天好得难以想象。

聚焦细看，令人惶恐；拉远视野，却无比美好。

当机械性工作被逐步取代，真正留下的，唯有意义。

要弄清自己一生真正想要什么，请选择一件你内心深处真正关切之事，以近乎冷酷的态度将其层层剖析，并毫不羞怯地向公众分享你的故事、价值观、愿景，以及与之相伴毕生投入的事业，从而构建一种类似手艺人般的生活方式——围绕着一小群真心支持你所做之事的人。再将这种生活方式与人工智能相结合，你便能腾出大量闲暇时光：这恰是对创造性工作的最高礼赞。

如何准备？

36个月，实现转变。

这个时限并非铁板钉钉，但已是目前你能获得的最贴近现实的数字。

你可以选择袖手旁观，继续沿袭旧日轨迹；也可以将此刻视为紧迫契机，彻底扭转人生方向。就我个人而言，实在想不出你为何不选择后者。重塑人生、为自己铺就非凡未来，并不需要你抛弃一切、远赴他乡；它只需要你重新选择自己的工作，需要你深入思考，需要你投身于一件你真正在意的事，需要你敢于冒险、打造一个值得讲述的故事，并把它分享给那些能从中获益的人。

过去构筑“美好生活”的一切要素，如今正逐一成为必备条件。

1）成为哲人型建造者  

当今世界，我们通常敬重两类人：  
程序员与营销人，宏观视野与技术细节，精神追求与务实行动，哲人与科学家。

而未来则要求我们弥合这些两极对立。建造者历来离不开思想者；缺乏营销思维的程序员，几乎注定无法吸引足够用户；沉溺于云端的理想主义者与困囿于原子的世界，同样都错失了真相。那些能同时承载这种二元性的个体，将势不可挡——而这一趋势，我们已然亲眼见证。

职位头衔正从“设计师”与“工程师”融合为“设计工程师”；各类工具——无论是否由AI驱动——已发展到这样的程度：人们无需额外增加工时，就能完成更多工作。

创作者正在创立并推动公司成长；程序员在社交媒体上动辄收获数百万浏览量。

人类能力的巅峰，在于成为一位“专精的通才”：既不能专精到稍有风吹草动即遭替代，或因过度绑定某种资质头衔而任人摆布；也不能泛泛而至，以致于样样涉猎、样样稀松，最终一事无成。

2）成为思想的过滤器  

如今，思想本身比执行更为重要。

【文章标题】你大约有36个月的时间来实现它  
【这是第5/5部分】

如果品味是新时代的智力，那么策展能力便是信息泛滥、人人皆可创作的世界里全新的“智商测试”——在这样一个时代，甄别哪些想法值得付诸实践，理应成为决策桌上的首要议题。

你的大脑必须进化为一台精密调校的“信噪比过滤器”。

要实现这一点，你首先需明白：你的大脑对现实的解读，取决于你的身份认同与世界观，取决于你的价值观与信念，取决于你奉行的生活准则，取决于你所处的发展阶段，也取决于你正努力实现的愿景。当接收到的信息有助于你达成核心且统摄全局的目标时，大脑便会释放多巴胺。

然而，由于大多数人要么根本没有明确目标，要么目标是由学校和工作强加给他们的，这一过程便变得异常痛苦。唯有那些决意反抗人生默认路径的人，才能开始锤炼自己的直觉，从而敏锐捕捉并有效运用那些面向未来的想法。

而判断哪些想法值得执行的唯一途径，就是在试错的烈火中锻造属于你自己的哲学。

3）成为人工智能的“指挥家”

采用人工智能时，首要且根本的抉择在于：何时借助AI，何时亲力亲为。

这一抉择通常取决于你真正享受做的事。对我而言，那就是写作。尽管我拥有一系列用于研究和构思的提示词（其中我最钟爱的一个，是让AI围绕我提供的主题不断提出观察性问题，直至我自己产生可用于写作的顿悟时刻），但我的所有书信均亲手撰写。AI于我而言，是一种增强写作能力的工具，而非取而代之的替代品。

在你的核心专长之外，我将AI提示词视作高度专业化的员工。我厌恶营销，因此我会用我所敬重的营销专家的资料训练AI，向它输入我的思维框架、范例或灵感来源，再让它生成初稿，最后由我依凭直觉与品味加以打磨。最终成稿质量更高，但与我亲自操刀所产出的内容并无本质区别。

深耕你的专长，同时统筹一支契合你价值观与愿景、富有品位的提示词“舰队”。

倘若你尚未开始尝试，学习AI的最佳方式，就是试着把自己从当前岗位上“自动化”地解放出来。

没错，这的确增加了你现有职位被取代的风险；但换个角度想，倘若某项工作本就可被自动化，那么你迟早会被取代——而主动拥抱自动化，至少能让你借此大幅提升能力，从而获得晋升机会，或具备独立执业的实力。

我将在后续的书信中继续深入探讨这些话题。

感谢你阅读这一封。

——丹
