articles.title: You can learn anything in 2 weeks
articles.description: 关于快速学习和掌握新技能的方法论。
articles.english:
You can learn anything in 2 weeks.

And no, I don’t mean you can become a master at any skill or topic. I mean you can acquire the specific knowledge necessary to get results toward a specific goal. And if that doesn’t make you extremely excited about how much you can speed up the progress you’re making toward the big milestones in your life – like making more money, acquiring a valuable skill, or learning a language, instrument, or software like After Effects – you may not be understanding what I’m saying just yet.

The problem is that people have become wired to think that success stems from 12+ hours of putting your nose in a textbook just to take an exam where 95% of the knowledge you’ve acquired goes out the window. And when it comes to getting real-world results, less than 1% of that knowledge applies.

In other words, you’re completely wasting most of the time you spend learning.

Schools train you to learn extremely slow. If learning allows you to be useful and get what you want, imagine what you could do if you spent time learning how to learn. You’d be able to achieve 10 goals in the time it takes the average person to achieve one.

In this letter, I want to show you exactly how to learn anything fast.

Skill acquisition = technique stacking

Everything you can do is a skill.

Does that not blow your mind?

That fact simplifies life quite a bit. The entire stoic philosophy of “control what you can control” is one of the few master keys that open the door of fulfillment. If you can’t control something, you can control your reaction to it. Therefore, that is a core skill for managing much of the pain in your life. If you can control something, then you can practice it to the point where it becomes so second nature to you that you learn to cut through reality with elegance and grace, like a guitarist who doesn’t have to expend much energy to nail a complex solo that leaves people in awe.

That said, most people try to acquire skills as a whole. That’s a massive disordered task. Choosing to “learn the guitar” is not clear. We’re talking about 5 years of extensive study and practice. There are tens of thousands of books, videos, articles, and people who want to tell you the “right way” to go about learning the guitar. They can’t teach you how to play the guitar, they can only teach you how they play the guitar.

So, how do we shortcut learning new skills? How do we cut through the noise and ensure we only learn what’s necessary? By understanding that skills are composed of techniques.

If I want to learn how to play the guitar, I don’t start learning.

I start playing. The entire purpose of learning the guitar is to play a song. That leads to step one: choose a song to play. Start with the purpose. But now you’re in a dilemma, you don’t know how to play the first note. That leads to step two: search for a resource that teaches you what that note is and the finger placements to play it. If you repeat that process of trial and error over a day or two, you’ll probably be able to play the song, even if it sounds terrible with lots of mistakes as you’re playing it.

The more you practice, the better you play that specific song.

When you move on to the next, you’ll realize that the various techniques you learned for that specific song – bar chords, mutes, etc – make it that much easier to learn faster.

As a more tangible example for creatives (most of you), take Photoshop.

While most people would go straight into watching an hour-long tutorial that goes over every single fucking tool in the sidebar, you start with what you want to do: create an image. You have no business learning Photoshop if you aren’t actively working toward a goal that requires it. You learn skills for utility, not entertainment, because you won’t actually learn the skill. Read a fiction book if you’re bored.

From there, you search for a specific technique, such as a series of steps to remove the background of a tree. Through your research, you find three different ways to select and mask an object (trees are particularly challenging to select, at least before Photoshop made removing the background a button-click away). You try them out, one technique works well, and you solidify that as a tool in your belt. With that alone, you’ve learned a critical puzzle piece in masking most things in Photoshop. As those techniques stack, you’ve not only saved countless hours of learning nonsense you won’t use, but you can effectively create most things you set your mind to.

Progressive overload of the mind

Skills are a group of neural pathways that form through repetition.

A technique we can think of as a single neural pathway. A single piece of the skill puzzle. When you collect enough pieces to the point of seeing 80% of the image, you can infer most of what you need to get results. If you understand a few techniques to speak Spanish, you can at least string a sentence together to get your point across. You may end up saying, “What can I buy water?” instead of “Where is the nearest place to buy water bottles?” but you’ll get the point across and accomplish your goal.

Let’s take a look at a more difficult example: making money.

Something everyone wants to do, but few people see as a skill that can be learned, because money (as with other life-changing skills like social dynamics) is deeply intertwined with our self-image, emotions, and survival. It’s difficult to see money as something within your direct control because we carry the burden of conditioning from our parents, teachers, and life experiences that influence our perception. We don’t control our reactions to impulses, so it creates a veil that disguises money as uncontrollable.

If you were to peel back all of the irrational thought barriers preventing you from execution and actually start doing the thing, you would realize that the ability to make more money can be learned quite fast. Not in a get-rich-quick scheme way, but in a way that’s similar to learning how to shoot a three-pointer. A beginner may have a 5% chance of making the shot out of luck, but a pro has a 99% chance without much effort at all.

You start with the purpose: make money. In order to do that, you need a product or service and a customer. You don’t have an idea for a product, so you look up a technique for finding a profitable idea, like in this mega guide for creating a product. If you continue to keep your mind at bay, you start building the product without spending a month questioning whether that idea is good, because ideas become clear with action. You don’t know how to attract customers, so you look up a technique and discover a few main options, such as social media content, paid ads, and direct outreach. You pick one. You try it. And while you may not be that great at it, you’re in luck, because you can simply continue to stack and test techniques, and if you solely focus on that, every technique you learn increases your earning potential.

If you want to bench press 315 pounds, you don’t throw that on the bar when you’ve never lifted a single weight in your life. Nor do you watch endless videos and expect them to teach you anything beyond the fundamentals that allow you to get started (you can watch a 3-minute video on that). Then you go to the fucking gym, put on weight, struggle to lift it, then come back a few days later and see if you can lift more.

Progressive overload.

The missing ingredient to learning absurdly fast

Rapid learning requires pure focus.

I don’t think many people in today’s world have experienced that.

P u r e f o c u s. Absolutely nothing else. You and the task. No thought. No distraction. A distraction is any person, place, or thing that pulls any thread of attention away from your goal. “You” literally cease to exist. You become one with reality. Input and output merge. Every slice of information that goes into your brain is instantly transformed into raw material that is put into reality like a lock and key.

You understand how to learn. You are close to tapping into this wonderful state of pure focus. Sometimes it happens naturally. You enter a period of intensity where your mind collapses on a clear goal. Pattern recognition kicks into overdrive. Books, content, music, and conversations gain an entirely new dimension. Reality becomes a source of inspiration as it always has been and will be, but you don’t have distractions pulling you away from that connection with what is.

Most of the time, this doesn’t happen at all. Learning is a boring grind. In that case, you may benefit from having AI coach you into a deep work session. But I do have one tool that I deploy when my mind is filled with dissonance – when I’m tired of where I am and almost clear on where I want to be.

That tool is what I call tactical stress. It is a form of environment engineering.

For myself, I was able to learn After Effects in about 2 weeks because I filled my YouTube video storyboard with animations I didn’t know how to make. I have to create videos each week. It’s a habit that allows me to survive. If I don’t put the video out, entropy releases, and the entirety of my work system starts to unravel. It’s much more painful than the process learning something to prevent that.

Tactical stress is when you put yourself in a high-pressure situation that creates a strong deadline to achieve the goal you’ve been meaning to achieve. Quitting your job to make your business work. Moving into an apartment you can’t afford to push for that new career. Saying “hi” to the person you’re attracted to so you have to at least start some kind of jumbled conversation. You either make it work, or you hesitate and get crushed. Tactical stress is so effective because most people tend to fall into the idle state. They numb themselves before they hit rock bottom, never allowing the pain of where they are to outweigh the pain of where they want to be. That’s when you deploy tactical stress. Right when you notice the pain of your current situation holding you back to avoid repeating the same 6 months for the rest of your life.

Put yourself in an environment that nearly forces you to learn what you need to learn, as fast as humanely possible, to achieve the goal that launches you into the next phase of life.

That, my friends, is how you learn.

– Dan
articles.chinese:
【文章标题】两周之内，你什么都能学会  
【这是第 1/4 部分】

两周之内，你什么都能学会。  

当然，我并不是说你能凭此成为任何技能或领域的专家。我的意思是：你完全可以在两周内掌握达成某一具体目标所必需的特定知识。如果你听完这句话，仍没有因意识到自己竟能如此大幅加速人生关键里程碑的进展——比如增加收入、习得一项高价值技能，或是掌握一门语言、一种乐器，又或是一款像 After Effects 这样的专业软件——而感到无比振奋，那很可能你还没真正理解我话中的深意。  

问题在于，人们早已被训练成这样一种思维模式：成功必须靠每天埋头苦读教科书十二小时以上，只为应付一场考试；而考完之后，你辛辛苦苦记住的九成五知识便瞬间烟消云散。至于在真实世界中产生实际成效，这些知识里能用上的还不到百分之一。  

换言之，你绝大多数的学习时间，其实都在白白浪费。  

学校教给你的，是一种极其低效的学习方式。倘若学习本身能让你变得更有能力、更能获得自己想要的东西，那么试想一下：如果你把一部分时间用来学习“如何学习”，你又能做到什么程度？你将能在普通人完成一个目标的时间里，高效达成十个目标。  

在这封信中，我想向你清晰展示：究竟该如何快速学会任何东西。  

技能习得 = 技术堆叠  

你所能做的一切，本质上都是一项技能。  

这个事实，难道不令你震撼？  

它的确大大简化了生活。“掌控你能掌控之事”——这句斯多葛哲学的核心信条，正是少数几把能开启人生满足之门的万能钥匙之一。倘若某件事你无法掌控，那你至少可以掌控自己对它的反应；因此，情绪调节便成了应对人生诸多痛苦的一项核心技能。而倘若某件事你本可掌控，那你就能通过反复练习，直至它成为你身体与意识的自然延伸——届时，你便能以优雅从容的姿态直面现实，如一位吉他手般，无需耗费多少心力，便能行云流水地奏出令人叹为观止的复杂独奏。  

然而，大多数人试图一次性掌握整项技能，这本身就是一项庞大而混乱的任务。“我要学吉他”这种目标，根本不够清晰——它意味着长达五年以上的系统学习与刻苦练习。市面上有数以万计的书籍、视频、文章，还有无数人争着告诉你“学吉他的正确方法”。但他们教不了你如何弹吉他，只能教你他们自己是如何弹吉他的。  

那么，我们该如何绕过弯路，快速掌握新技能？又该如何拨开信息噪音，确保只学真正必需的内容？答案是：认清一个基本事实——所有技能，均由一系列具体技术构成。  

如果我想学会弹吉他，我不会一上来就“开始学”。

【文章标题】两周内，你可以学会任何技能  
【这是第2/4部分】

我开始演奏。学习吉他的全部目的，就是为了弹奏一首歌。这便引出了第一步：选择一首你想弹的歌。从最终目标出发。但此时你陷入了困境——你连第一个音符都不会弹。这就引出了第二步：寻找一份教学资源，告诉你这个音符是什么、手指该如何摆放才能弹出它。如果你花一两天时间反复尝试、不断纠错，很可能就能把这首歌弹出来，哪怕听起来糟糕透顶，演奏过程中错误百出。

练习得越多，你对这首特定歌曲的演奏水平就越高。

当你转向下一首歌时，便会发现：之前为掌握那首歌而习得的各种技巧——比如横按和闷音等——会让你学得更快、更轻松。

再举一个对创意工作者（也就是在座各位中的大多数）而言更具体、更贴切的例子：Photoshop。

大多数人会直接点开一段长达一小时的教程视频，逐个讲解侧边栏里每一个该死的工具；而你则应从自己真正想做的事入手：制作一张图像。如果你没有明确的目标需要借助Photoshop来实现，那么学习它根本毫无意义。你学技能是为了实用，而非消遣；否则，你实际上根本学不会这项技能。要是觉得无聊，不如去读一本小说。

接下来，你便有针对性地搜索某项具体技术，例如“如何去除一棵树的背景”。通过查阅资料，你发现有三种不同的方法可用于选中并蒙版化某个对象（树木尤其难选——至少在Photoshop将“一键去背景”变成现实之前是这样）。你逐一尝试，其中一种方法效果显著，于是你便把它稳稳纳入自己的技能工具箱。仅凭这一招，你就已掌握了Photoshop中绝大多数蒙版操作的关键拼图之一。随着这类技巧不断累积，你不仅省下了无数小时去学习那些永远用不上的冗余知识，更能高效实现自己心中构想的绝大多数创作目标。

心智的渐进式超负荷训练

技能，本质上是一组经由重复练习而形成的神经通路。

我们可以把某项具体技术视作一条单一的神经通路，即构成整项技能的一块拼图。当你收集到足够多的拼图，使整体图像呈现达八成左右时，你便能据此推断出达成目标所需的大部分内容。比如，你若掌握了几种基础的西班牙语表达技巧，至少就能组织起一个句子，把自己的意思传达出去。你或许会说：“我能买水吗？”而不是“最近哪里可以买到瓶装水？”，但你的意图已然清晰，目标也顺利达成。

我们再来看一个更难的例子：赚钱。

【文章标题】两周内，你可以学会任何技能  
【这是第3/4部分】

人人都想掌握理财能力，却极少有人将其视为一项可通过学习获得的技能——因为金钱（如同社交能力等其他能彻底改变人生的技能）与我们的自我形象、情绪乃至生存本能紧密交织。我们很难将金钱视作自己可直接掌控的事物，因为我们背负着来自父母、老师以及过往人生经历的深层条件反射，这些因素持续塑造着我们对金钱的认知。我们无法自主调控自己对冲动的反应，于是便形成了一层认知迷雾，使金钱看似不可控。

倘若你能层层剥开所有阻碍行动的非理性思维障碍，真正开始动手去做，便会发现：提升收入的能力其实可以学得非常快。这并非什么“一夜暴富”的捷径，而更像学习投三分球——初学者可能仅凭运气有5%的命中率，而职业球员几乎不费吹灰之力，命中率就高达99%。

你从明确目标开始：赚钱。要实现这一点，你需要一个产品或服务，以及一个客户。你暂时还没有产品创意？那就去查阅一套行之有效的创意挖掘方法，比如这份详尽的产品开发指南。只要你不再让疑虑牵绊住自己，就能立刻着手打造产品，而不会花上整整一个月反复纠结“这个点子到底好不好”——因为想法只有在行动中才会逐渐清晰。你还不懂如何吸引客户？那就去查找相关方法，很快就会发现几条主流路径：社交媒体内容运营、付费广告投放、直接联系潜在客户。你只需从中选一种，立即尝试。即便起初效果平平，也无需担心——你完全可以持续叠加并测试不同方法；只要你全神贯注于这一过程，每掌握一项新技巧，你的创收潜力就随之提升一分。

如果你想卧推315磅，绝不会在从未碰过哑铃的情况下，直接把杠铃片堆满杠铃杆。同样，你也不会无休止地刷教学视频，指望它们教会你远超基础入门的知识（事实上，关于卧推的基本要点，三分钟视频足矣）。接着，你就该直奔健身房，加上重量，咬牙举起，哪怕艰难挣扎；几天后再回来，看看能否多举起一点。

渐进式超负荷训练。

快速掌握一切的关键缺失要素。

高效学习，需要的是纯粹的专注。

我想，当今世界中，真正体验过这种状态的人并不多。

纯·粹·专·注。除此之外，别无他物。只有你与任务本身。没有杂念，没有干扰。“干扰”指任何分散你一丝一毫注意力的人、地点或事物。“你”这个概念甚至暂时消解——你与现实融为一体。输入与输出合二为一。涌入大脑的每一丝信息，都会即刻转化为可投入现实的原始素材，严丝合缝，如锁配钥。

【文章标题】你可以在两周内学会任何东西  
【这是第 4/4 部分】

你已懂得如何学习。你离进入那种纯粹专注的奇妙状态，仅一步之遥。有时，这种状态会自然降临：你进入一段高度投入的时期，心神凝聚于一个清晰的目标之上；模式识别能力随之全速启动；书籍、内容、音乐乃至日常对话，都焕发出前所未有的深度与意义；现实本身重新成为灵感的源泉——它本就如此，也永远如此——而你不再被各种干扰拉扯，从而得以持续沉浸于对“当下实相”的真切联结之中。

但大多数时候，这种状态压根不会出现。学习变成了一件枯燥乏味的苦差事。此时，你或许可以从人工智能教练那里获得帮助，助你进入深度工作状态。不过，我倒有一个自己常用的工具，专用于应对内心充满矛盾与撕裂感的时刻——当你对现状感到厌倦，同时又几乎明确知道自己真正想去往何方之时。

这个工具，我称之为“战术性压力”，本质上是一种环境设计策略。

对我而言，之所以能在约两周内掌握After Effects，正是因为我在YouTube视频分镜脚本中，刻意加入了大量自己尚不会制作的动画效果。我每周必须产出视频，这早已成为维系我职业生存的习惯。一旦视频无法如期发布，“熵增”便会爆发，整个工作系统随之迅速瓦解。这种崩塌带来的痛苦，远比为避免它而主动学习新技能的过程更令人难以承受。

所谓“战术性压力”，就是主动将自己置于高压情境之中，人为制造一个强有力的截止期限，以推动自己完成那个早已心向往之却迟迟未行动的目标：比如辞去现有工作，孤注一掷地经营自己的事业；搬进一间经济上难以负担的公寓，以此倒逼自己快速转入理想的新职业轨道；又或者，鼓起勇气向心仪之人打声招呼，哪怕只是开启一段语无伦次的对话——你唯有奋力达成目标，否则便只能踌躇不前，最终被现实碾碎。战术性压力之所以极为有效，是因为多数人习惯滑入无所作为的惰性状态：他们往往在触底之前就选择自我麻痹，从未让“现状之痛”真正压过“愿景之痛”。而战术性压力，正是在你猛然察觉——当前处境所带来的痛苦，正拖住你的脚步，使你恐惧未来数月甚至数年都将困在原地、重复同样的循环——那一刻，果断启用。

请主动将自己置于一种近乎强制性的环境中：在那里，你不得不以人类所能达到的最快速度，掌握那些实现跃迁所必需的知识与技能——因为唯有如此，你才能抵达人生下一阶段的起点。

朋友们，这就是你学会一切的方式。

——丹

articles.title: These 3 Decisions Will Determine If You Get Rich
articles.description: 分析如何通过设定妄想型目标来重新重构大脑认知。
articles.english:
The only way to get rich is to (1) value your time at a delusional dollar amount, (2) be obsessed with getting rich, and (3) give yourself no other option but to get rich.

Now, I know there are a few people in the back screaming that “money isn’t everything!” or regurgitating a shallow “money doesn’t buy happiness” they got from someone who doesn’t understand money or happiness, but this letter is for those who didn’t just click on this to get angry and completely waste their time.

This letter is for those who want to get unapologetically rich.

Not because you’re a terrible and evil person, but because the only other option in your head is to be valued at what the market thinks you’re worth, and that’s terrifying.

For myself, I realized early in my life that I was not okay with breaking my back for 8-10 hours a day to make $80-$150,000 a year in a job where I own nothing doing work I don’t care about, especially when I can see as clear as day that there are people doing meaningful work who make 100x that amount while working a fraction of the time.

I may not have had the value to make that much when I was young, obviously, but I knew it was possible.

I knew that there was a series of decisions I could make that would lead to me having so much control over my money that it no longer dominated my mind, emotions, or time. People who endlessly moralize and spiritualize money can’t fathom a life where they aren’t bound to it.

While I can’t tell you exactly what to do (I mean, I can, but reality’s outputs vary depending on the person), I can give you 3 ways to rewire your brain to the point of making the right decisions that lead to you getting rich.

In other words, I can install the beliefs in your mind that help you test the inputs that are much more likely to get reality to spit out wealth as a result.

The aspirational hourly rate

Set and enforce an aspirational hourly rate. If fixing a problem will save less than your rate, ignore it. If outsourcing a task will cost less than your hourly rate, outsource it… My aspirational rate was $5,000/hr.

— Naval Ravikant

This will baffle most people (it would surely baffle my past self), but I’m at a point where someone could offer me $5,000 for a one-on-one call and I wouldn’t do it. Not because I couldn’t use the money or I don’t want to help people, but because there is time, focus, and the obligation to deliver $5k worth of value on the line. That’s a big responsibility that demands that I prioritize it above other potentially more rewarding things.

It would be stupid for me to split my focus when I know exactly what to do to make more than that in an hour.

The purpose of setting an aspirational hourly rate is just that: to make better decisions and frame your mind to notice the opportunities that put you in a place of higher leverage.

Let’s imagine you purchased a $50 item that was defective or broken. Would you go through the hour of trouble to return it? If so, you value your time at $50 an hour, if not less. That’s not a “bad” thing, but it shines the light of awareness on a more important fact: you aren’t conscious of a problem you could be working on that would lead to you making $500 – or $5000 – within that same hour. If you were, it wouldn’t make sense to spend that hour returning the item.

If your aspirational hourly rate doesn’t feel impossible, it’s too low.

Why?

Delusional goals rewire your brain.

Your brain is literally reshaping itself right now based on what you’re learning and thinking about, this letter included. When you imagine a better future, it activates the same brain networks as if you were experiencing them. Every single moment of focused attention is a chance to rewire your brain in alignment with the person you want to become. That’s one of many reasons doomscrollers and those who don’t manage their inputs (mental or physical) are digging their own grave one moment at a time.

Beyond that, dopamine spikes more during goal pursuit than achievement. But that’s where it gets dangerous. Visualizing your goals all day enhances learning, but only if you pair it with an optimal level of challenge from real-world scenarios. Being in the game. Otherwise, it just turns into mental masturbation: telling everyone about your goals to get a cheap dopamine hit but never actually doing anything about it.

The golden zone for challenge is about 85% difficulty. Not so high that you get anxious, but not so low that you get bored. The stress from the progressive overload of challenge releases norepinephrine, which enhances learning further and helps you adapt into that new state of mind.

So, you can’t just think about your aspirational hourly rate and pray that you make more money.

You need to make difficult decisions with your rate in mind.

Start by not returning the item.

You’ll be fine.

Concentration of force is the only way to get rich

If you want to get rich, it needs to be your number one overwhelming desire.

At least until the actions of getting rich are so deeply engrained in your psyche that you don’t need to expend much mental energy to perform them, like a professional basketball player who doesn’t need to think about hitting 3 pointers on command.

This holds true for anything you want to be successful at: concentration of force is the only way to become the person who achieves big goals. You need to be obsessed. You need to channel as much energy as possible into that goal.

But what about going out? Enjoying life? Being social? Chasing the western version of happiness (an impossibly sustained state of euphoria)?

Well, you’re not going to create wealth because it’s not your priority. And that’s perfectly fine. You don’t need to have the goal of getting rich, but many people do, and they’re just as wrong as you about the meaning of life, and someone without that as their priority isn’t going to accidentally get rich. A side goal of investing a few bucks in the stock market over the next 40 years is one way to enjoy a decent amount of money later in your life, but who in their right mind wouldn’t want that much money, and more, 30 years earlier if they had the knowledge to do so?

Oh, by the way, getting rich as a priority doesn’t make life worse, it makes it infinitely better.

Does a professional athlete have a terrible life? Probably not, they’re doing what they love, most of the time. So why do you not apply the same logic to business? Can someone not have a good life while attempting to perform at the peak of their abilities in the domain they choose?

One could argue that happiness is the combination of progress being made and contribution to something greater than yourself, so when you aren’t distracted from that progress and are solving valuable problems at scale (that’s what entrepreneurship is), life is a thousand times more enjoyable than the average.

Yes, you’ll still have to do things that life requires, but it will cause you pain to do so. That pain is how you orient your decision-making. Because the more you tolerate it, the less you act to change it.

To make this tangible, start by creating a list of things you don’t do.

Things that are literally not worth your time. Coffee meetings. Returning stupid items. Scrolling because you’re bored. Partying because you lack zest and proper stimulation. Texting everyone back on time (this one is especially stupid, because nobody is wired for people being able to access their attention at any time). Little todos that could be outsourced or ignored. When these decisions come up, firmly state, “I don’t do that.”

Then, create a list of things you will do.

Things that merge your real hourly rate with your aspirational hourly rate. Study information that drastically increases your earning potential. Practice skills that make you self-reliant. Starting a business. Joining a startup. Pushing for an executive role. Learning and building.

The more you think about your actions, the easier it is to see why you aren’t rich.

Give yourself no other option but to succeed

The best decisions I’ve made always involved using my money as a forcing function to make more.

In other words, I invested in things I couldn’t afford, and I learned to trust myself to make it back that much faster.

The first significant spike in my income occurred after I purchased an email marketing and product hosting software for $1,500. At the time, that money was precious to me. It deeply pained me to spend that money. I felt that spike of anxiety when I hit “purchase.” But that pain drove me to attempt to make that money back as if my life depended on it. It forced me to learn how to make the most of it with marketing, copywriting, and funnel knowledge. With that one purchase, I didn’t have to guess what “high-value” skills to learn. It was obvious that if I learned them, I would increase my earning potential.

The same thing happened when I consistently moved into various apartments. Each one more expensive than the next. Each one costing more than I was comfortable with. On the surface, it looked like I was just another victim of lifestyle creep. In reality, it was a real-world way of imposing a deadline on a challenge that I knew I could take on. I was physically putting myself in the environment of my future self, and I didn’t have the option to stay in the life I no longer wanted.

Those 3 decisions – an aspirational hourly rate, concentration of force, and giving myself no other option but to succeed – created the perfect conditions to make more money than my younger self thought was possible.

None of those decisions involved obsessing over “what skill to learn” or “what business model to choose.” I didn’t have time to think about that. I had to learn it all.

Of course, it took a lot of failure and iteration, but this is social media, who talks about that stuff ;)? And while I’m not a proponent of getting rich quick, you’d be surprised how fast you can if you set the right conditions as outlined in this letter. In fact, I’d argue that you can learn any skill (and be better at it than 99% of people) in 2 weeks.

I’ll save that for another letter.

Thank you for reading this one.

– Dan

If you want to learn the skills that prepare you for the future, consider joining the paid tier of my substack. It has a skill library with various AI prompts, writing strategies, marketing strategies, and a full one-person business course.The only way to get rich is to (1) value your time at a delusional dollar amount, (2) be obsessed with getting rich, and (3) give yourself no other option but to get rich.

【文章标题】这三个决定将决定你能否致富  
【这是第 1/4 部分】

致富的唯一途径在于：（1）以近乎狂妄的金额来衡量你的时间价值；（2）对致富抱有近乎偏执的专注；（3）彻底斩断所有退路，只留下“必须致富”这一条出路。

我知道，此刻或许有人在角落里高声喊着“金钱不是万能的！”——或者机械地复述一句肤浅的陈词滥调：“金钱买不到幸福”。可这话偏偏出自那些既不懂金钱、也不懂幸福的人之口。但本信并非写给这类人；它不为激怒读者而存在，更无意让任何人白白浪费宝贵时间。

这封信，是写给那些渴望毫无愧疚、理直气壮地变得富有的人。

你追求财富，并非因为你是个糟糕而邪恶的人，而是因为在你的认知中，另一种可能——即任由市场来定义你的价值——实在令人恐惧。

就我自己而言，很早便意识到：我无法接受每天辛劳八到十小时，只为换来一份年薪八万至十五万美元的工作——这份工作我既不拥有任何权益，所做之事也与我毫无共鸣。尤其当我清楚看到，有人正从事真正有意义的工作，却能在远少得多的工时内，赚取百倍于此的收入。

年轻时的我，当然尚不具备匹配如此高收入的价值，这一点我心知肚明；但我坚信，这种可能性真实存在。

我深知，只要做出一系列关键决策，就能逐步掌控自己的财富，直至它不再主宰我的思绪、情绪与时间。而那些终日用道德或灵性去粉饰金钱的人，根本无法想象一种挣脱金钱束缚的人生。

我虽不能手把手告诉你该具体怎么做（严格来说，我其实可以给出建议，但现实结果因人而异），却能为你提供三种重塑思维模式的方法——助你持续作出通向财富的关键决策。

换言之，我能帮你植入一些核心信念，使你得以主动测试那些更有可能让现实“吐出”财富的行动方案。

**理想化时薪**

设定并坚决执行一个理想化的时薪标准：若解决某个问题所能节省的成本低于你的时薪，那就直接忽略；若外包某项任务的成本低于你的时薪，那就果断外包……我的理想化时薪定为每小时5000美元。

——纳瓦尔·拉维坎特

这会让大多数人感到震惊（当年的我肯定也会目瞪口呆），但如今，哪怕有人愿付我5000美元进行一次一对一咨询，我也不会答应。原因并非我不需要这笔钱，也绝非不愿助人，而是因为一旦应允，我就必须投入相应的时间、保持高度专注，并切实交付价值等同于5000美元的服务成果——这是一份沉甸甸的责任，要求我将其置于其他一切潜在回报更高的事务之上。

当我已明确知道如何在一小时内创造远超此数的收益时，再分散精力去做别的事，无疑是愚蠢的。

设定理想化时薪的根本目的，正在于此：优化决策质量，并重塑思维框架，让你敏锐识别那些能大幅提升自身杠杆效应的机会。

【文章标题】这三个决定将决定你能否致富  
【这是第 2/4 部分】

假设你花50美元买了一件有缺陷或已损坏的商品。你会花整整一小时去退换它吗？如果你会，那就说明你将自己的时间价值定为每小时50美元，甚至更低。这本身并非“不好”，但它却照亮了一个更关键的事实：你并未意识到，自己本可在同一小时内着手解决某个问题——而这个问题的解决，可能为你带来500美元，甚至5000美元的收入。倘若你真意识到了这一点，那花一小时去退换商品便毫无道理可言。

如果你所憧憬的时薪听起来并不遥不可及，那这个目标就定得太低了。

为什么？

不切实际的目标，会重塑你的大脑。

你的大脑此刻正实实在在地依据你所学、所思的内容（包括这封信在内）进行自我重塑。当你构想一个更美好的未来时，激活的大脑神经网络，与你真正身临其境时完全相同。每一次专注的凝神，都是一个契机——让你的大脑朝着你想成为的那个自己，重新布线。这也是为何那些沉溺于末日式刷屏、以及无法管理自身信息输入（无论是心理层面还是物理层面）的人，正一点一滴地亲手为自己掘墓。

此外，多巴胺在追逐目标的过程中激增的程度，远超目标达成之时。但恰恰是这一点，潜藏着危险。整天幻想自己的目标固然能促进学习，但前提是——你必须同步置身于真实世界中，迎接恰到好处的挑战。也就是说，你得真正“上场参赛”。否则，这种幻想只会沦为精神自慰：向所有人高谈阔论你的目标，只为获取廉价的多巴胺快感，却从未付诸任何实际行动。

挑战的黄金区间，难度约为85%：既不能高到令你焦虑不安，也不能低到让你感到无聊乏味。随着挑战难度循序渐进地提升，身体产生的压力会释放去甲肾上腺素，从而进一步强化学习效果，并助你顺利适应这种崭新的思维状态。

因此，光是想想自己理想中的时薪，然后祈祷收入自然增长，是行不通的。

你必须以这个时薪为标尺，做出艰难的抉择。

第一步，就是别去退换那件商品。

你完全没问题。

聚焦力量，是致富的唯一途径

若想致富，它就必须成为你压倒一切、至高无上的渴望。

至少，在致富所需的一系列行动尚未深深融入你的潜意识之前，你需要如此；直到这些行动变得如同职业篮球运动员投三分球一般——无需刻意思考，即可信手拈来。

这一原则适用于你渴望在任何领域取得成功的所有目标：唯有聚焦力量，才能蜕变为那个真正实现宏大目标的人。你必须为之痴迷，必须倾注尽可能多的能量于这一目标之上。

但社交聚会呢？享受生活呢？维系人际关系呢？追求西方语境下那种幸福——一种永续不衰、极致亢奋的状态呢？

【文章标题】这三个决定将决定你能否致富  
【这是第3/4部分】

好吧，你不会创造财富，因为那根本不是你的优先事项。这完全没问题。你不必以“致富”为目标，但许多人的确以此为目标；而他们对生命意义的理解，和你一样存在偏差。同样，若致富并非某人的首要目标，那么他绝不会“偶然”变得富有。未来四十年里，在股市中零星投入一点钱，作为一项附带目标，的确能让你晚年拥有一笔可观的收入；但试问，倘若你掌握了相应知识，谁又不想在三十年前就早早获得这笔钱，甚至更多呢？

哦，顺带一提：把致富当作优先事项，并不会让生活变得更糟，反而会让它变得无比美好。

职业运动员的生活很糟糕吗？大概率并非如此——他们大多时候都在做自己热爱的事。那么，你为何不将同样的逻辑套用到商业领域呢？一个人难道不能一边竭尽所能、在自己选择的领域中追求卓越，一边依然过上充实而美好的生活吗？

有人或许会说，幸福源于两者的结合：一是切实感受到自身在进步，二是为超越自我的某种更大价值作出贡献。因此，当你不再被琐事分心，而是专注于规模化地解决真正有价值的问题（而这正是创业的本质），你的生活体验将比普通人高出千倍。

当然，你仍需完成生活中那些不得不做的事，但这些事会给你带来痛苦。而这种痛苦，恰恰是你校准决策方向的标尺——因为你越是容忍它，就越少主动去改变现状。

为了让这一理念更具体可感，请先列出一份“你坚决不做”的事项清单：

那些真正不值得你耗费时间的事：毫无意义的咖啡会谈；退回无脑的商品；因无聊而刷手机；因缺乏活力与恰当刺激而硬撑着参加派对；事无巨细、及时回复每一条信息（尤其荒谬的是，没人天生就该随时待命、任人随意攫取自己的注意力）；本可外包或直接忽略的小任务。每当这类事情浮现时，请坚定地说：“我不做这个。”

接着，再列出一份“你决心去做”的事项清单：

那些能将你当前真实时薪与理想时薪真正融合起来的事：研习能大幅提高你收入潜力的知识；锤炼让你真正自立自足的技能；创办一家企业；加入一家初创公司；争取高管职位；持续学习并动手创造。

你越深入反思自己的行为，就越容易看清自己为何至今尚未致富。

只给自己留下“成功”这一条路

我做过的最明智的决定，往往都涉及将金钱当作一种“倒逼机制”，迫使自己采取更积极的行动。

换言之，我曾投资于自己当时根本负担不起的东西，并学会相信自己——相信自己能更快地把这笔钱赚回来。

【文章标题】这三个决定将决定你能否致富  
【这是第4/4部分】

我收入的首次显著增长，发生在我花1500美元购买了一套电子邮件营销与产品托管软件之后。当时，这笔钱对我来说极为珍贵，掏出去时内心十分煎熬；点击“购买”按钮的那一刻，焦虑感骤然涌上心头。但正是这种痛感，驱使我拼尽全力去把钱赚回来——仿佛我的人生全系于此。它迫使我深入学习如何最大化利用这套工具：钻研营销、苦练文案写作、掌握销售漏斗设计。仅凭这一次投入，我便无需再费神猜测究竟该学哪些“高价值”技能——答案一目了然：只要掌握了这些，我的收入潜力必将大幅提升。

同样的逻辑也体现在我持续更换公寓的经历中。每一次我都搬进更贵的住所，租金一次比一次超出我的心理舒适区。表面上看，我不过是“生活方式通胀”的又一个受害者；实际上，这却是我在现实世界中为自身设定挑战期限的一种方式——一个我确信自己有能力应对的挑战。我实实在在地把自己置身于未来那个“理想自我”所处的环境中，而旧有的生活，已不再是我能容忍停留的地方。

上述三个决定——确立一个令人向往的时薪标准、集中全部精力攻坚、以及彻底斩断所有退路、只留成功这一条道——共同营造出最有利于增收的条件，其结果远超年轻时的我所能想象。

这三项决定，没有一项是围绕“该学什么技能”或“该选哪种商业模式”反复纠结。我没空琢磨这些——我必须边干边学，全部掌握。

当然，过程中充斥着大量失败与反复试错；但这是社交媒体时代，谁会聊这些呢？；）诚然，我并不鼓吹“一夜暴富”，但如果你按本文所述的方式，为自己设定恰当的前提条件，你会惊讶于财富积累的速度之快。事实上，我甚至敢说：任何一项技能，你都能在两周内掌握，并且达到超越99%普通人的水平。

这点，我留待下一封信再详述。

感谢你读完这一封。

——丹

如果你想掌握面向未来的核心能力，欢迎订阅我的Substack付费会员。会员专属内容包括：技能资源库（涵盖各类AI提示词、写作策略、营销策略），以及一套完整的“单人创业全流程课程”。  
致富的唯一路径在于：（1）以近乎狂妄的金额来定义你的时间价值；（2）对致富抱持一种近乎偏执的专注；（3）彻底关闭所有退路，唯以致富为唯一选项。

sentences.english: The only way to get rich is to (1) value your time at a delusional dollar amount, (2) be obsessed with getting rich, and (3) give yourself no other option but to get rich.
sentences.chinese: 致富的唯一途径是：（1）以近乎狂妄的美元金额来衡量你的时间价值；（2）对致富极度痴迷；（3）彻底切断所有退路，只允许自己成功。

sentences.english: This letter is for those who want to get unapologetically rich.
sentences.chinese: 这封信写给那些想理直气壮、毫无愧疚地变得富有的人。

sentences.english: Not because you’re a terrible and evil person, but because the only other option in your head is to be valued at what the market thinks you’re worth, and that’s terrifying.
sentences.chinese: 这并非因为你是个糟糕或邪恶的人，而是因为在你的认知中，另一种选择就是任由市场决定你的价值——而这令人恐惧。

sentences.english: I was not okay with breaking my back for 8–10 hours a day to make $80–$150,000 a year in a job where I own nothing doing work I don’t care about.
sentences.chinese: 我无法接受每天辛劳8–10小时，只为在一份我毫无所有权、也毫无热情的工作中赚取8万–15万美元年薪。

sentences.english: There are people doing meaningful work who make 100x that amount while working a fraction of the time.
sentences.chinese: 确实有人从事有意义的工作，收入是那个数字的100倍，而工作时间却只是其中一小部分。

sentences.english: I knew that there was a series of decisions I could make that would lead to me having so much control over my money that it no longer dominated my mind, emotions, or time.
sentences.chinese: 我深知，只要做出一系列关键决策，就能彻底掌控金钱——让它不再主宰我的思想、情绪或时间。

sentences.english: People who endlessly moralize and spiritualize money can’t fathom a life where they aren’t bound to it.
sentences.chinese: 那些不断将金钱道德化、灵性化的人，根本无法想象一种不被金钱束缚的生活。

sentences.english: Set and enforce an aspirational hourly rate.
sentences.chinese: 设定并严格执行一个‘理想化’的时薪标准。

sentences.english: If fixing a problem will save less than your rate, ignore it.
sentences.chinese: 如果解决某个问题所节省的钱少于你的时薪，那就直接忽略它。

sentences.english: If outsourcing a task will cost less than your hourly rate, outsource it.
sentences.chinese: 如果外包某项任务的成本低于你的时薪，那就果断外包。

sentences.english: My aspirational rate was $5,000/hr.
sentences.chinese: 我设定的理想时薪是每小时5000美元。

sentences.english: That’s a big responsibility that demands that I prioritize it above other potentially more rewarding things.
sentences.chinese: 这是一份重大责任，要求我必须将其优先级置于其他可能更有回报的事情之上。

sentences.english: The purpose of setting an aspirational hourly rate is just that: to make better decisions and frame your mind to notice the opportunities that put you in a place of higher leverage.
sentences.chinese: 设定理想时薪的目的正在于此：帮你做出更优决策，并重塑思维模式，从而敏锐识别能带来更高杠杆效应的机会。

sentences.english: If your aspirational hourly rate doesn’t feel impossible, it’s too low.
sentences.chinese: 如果你的理想时薪听起来并不‘不可能’，那它就定得太低了。

sentences.english: Delusional goals rewire your brain.
sentences.chinese: 看似狂妄的目标，恰恰能重塑你的大脑神经回路。

sentences.english: When you imagine a better future, it activates the same brain networks as if you were experiencing them.
sentences.chinese: 当你构想更美好的未来时，大脑中被激活的神经网络，与你真实经历该未来时完全相同。

sentences.english: Every single moment of focused attention is a chance to rewire your brain in alignment with the person you want to become.
sentences.chinese: 每一次专注的凝神，都是重塑大脑、使之趋近理想自我的一次机会。

sentences.english: Dopamine spikes more during goal pursuit than achievement.
sentences.chinese: 多巴胺的峰值往往出现在追逐目标的过程中，而非达成目标的那一刻。

sentences.english: Visualizing your goals all day enhances learning, but only if you pair it with an optimal level of challenge from real-world scenarios.
sentences.chinese: 整天设想目标确实能促进学习，但前提是必须搭配来自现实场景的适度挑战。

sentences.english: The golden zone for challenge is about 85% difficulty.
sentences.chinese: 挑战的‘黄金区间’难度约为85%——既不会高到引发焦虑，也不会低到让人厌倦。

sentences.english: Concentration of force is the only way to get rich.
sentences.chinese: 集中全部力量，是致富的唯一路径。

sentences.english: It needs to be your number one overwhelming desire.
sentences.chinese: 它必须成为你压倒一切的首要渴望。

sentences.english: You need to be obsessed. You need to channel as much energy as possible into that goal.
sentences.chinese: 你必须对此痴迷，并将尽可能多的能量倾注于这一目标。

sentences.english: Start by creating a list of things you don’t do.
sentences.chinese: 先从列出‘你坚决不做’的事情开始。

sentences.english: Things that are literally not worth your time: coffee meetings, returning stupid items, scrolling because you’re bored.
sentences.chinese: 那些真正不值得你投入时间的事：闲聊式咖啡会面、为小物件费力退货、因无聊而无意识刷屏。

sentences.english: Firmly state, 'I don’t do that.'
sentences.chinese: 坚定地说：‘这事我不做。’

sentences.english: Create a list of things you will do — things that merge your real hourly rate with your aspirational hourly rate.
sentences.chinese: 再列出‘你一定要做’的事——那些能将你当前实际时薪与理想时薪真正融合起来的行动。

sentences.english: The more you think about your actions, the easier it is to see why you aren’t rich.
sentences.chinese: 你越深入反思自己的行为，就越容易看清自己为何尚未致富。

sentences.english: I invested in things I couldn’t afford, and I learned to trust myself to make it back that much faster.
sentences.chinese: 我投资于自己当时负担不起的东西，并学会相信自己能更快地把钱赚回来。

sentences.english: I was physically putting myself in the environment of my future self, and I didn’t have the option to stay in the life I no longer wanted.
sentences.chinese: 我实实在在地把自己置身于未来自我的环境中，而我已没有退路，无法继续留在那个我不再想要的人生里。

articles.title: 20-30 Years Old Is The Tutorial Phase, Don’t F*ck It Up
articles.description: 给年轻人的生活建议：避开三件事，坚持做三件事。
articles.english:
This letter is going to piss some people off because it’s for a specific type of person.

I’m going to sound like an inconsiderate asshole to most people but that’s the only way I can get the severity of this situation across.

With that said, consider nuance turned off as of right now.

The people who get angry at the brutal honesty here are often those who have pretty terrible lives. They haven’t grown as a person past the age of 20 to 25.

They are the people who never realized this:

The best way to make the most of your 20s is to make them your worst.

You see, you have two options:

Use your 20s to become who you were meant to be.

Repeat the same 6 months for the entirety of your life.

If you don’t nearly max out your potential in your 20s, you can simply observe society and see that you become like everyone else.

You get stuck in a loop of anxiety, overwhelm, and attempting to live your last peak experience. You go to the same bars and raves. You play the same video games. You have the best experience of your life because you’re old enough to do new things, but not wise enough to realize that those are the lowest peaks one can experience, so you fill your life with those shallow activities.

Most people plateau around 23 years old.

When you ask them what they’re doing with their life, in an honest way, they don’t have anything to tell you, so they confidently say they’re “just living life.”

The thing is, you don’t realize the ramifications of staying the same.

If you did, you’d have no option but to change.

Most people turn 30 years old with the emotional maturity of a 15-year-old. The world rapidly pushes forward while your mind, body, spirit, and finances stay in place. But that’s the problem. Staying the same is an illusion. Without trying, you slowly dig yourself into a mediocre hole that only becomes more difficult to climb out of.

Your 20s are the tutorial, not the game.

The preparation, not the main event.

So, here are 3 traps to avoid, and 3 ways to turn it all around.

If you can set yourself up in your 20s, your quality of life will only continue to increase, even when your youth is no longer on your side.

Don’t listen to anyone who doesn’t have the life you want.

People who have the life you want are rare.

1% of the population.

Possibly less.

The other 99% are people who love to blabber about how you should live your life when they wasted their own. They didn’t achieve anything great, so they are adamant on convincing you that the greatest things to do in life are the greatest things they did, which aren’t great at all.

They will tell you to be more realistic. Aim lower. Be like them. Enjoy your 20s! Get the job. Create a budget. Invest your measly savings. Live a boring and mechanical life doing work you hate until you turn 50, as if it’s some twisted rite of passage. Many people say they want the best for you, but in reality, they don’t want to feel inferior to you.

The people who have the life you want are often quiet.

They are difficult to find.

Keep an eye out for them.

For most people, taking your parents, teachers, or peers’ advice to heart is a death sentence.

Get your taste of distractions, fast.

Most people treat their youth as a currency instead of investment capital.

They party. They smoke. And while those things aren’t the end of the world in and of themselves, they destroy the immense benefits of being young: time, energy, focus.

I was a dumb college kid too, but I always had something to work on that would someday “buy my freedom.”

I’m not telling you to avoid those things altogether. In fact, you would benefit from getting a taste of them quickly so you can recognize them as mistakes. Instead, I’m telling you to have a life-altering goal that demands you at your best so you notice the impact of your degeneracy.

The average person doesn’t see the problem with drinking and smoking because their life doesn’t demand a high level of performance. They work a desk job they’d rather not be at, so the hangover and laziness don’t really matter.

However, those aren’t the only social distractions.

I understand that you’re a young person who wants to experience the world and has their hormones obliterated from birth control and environmental toxins, but no, you aren’t going to meet the love of your life when you’re the worst version of yourself.

If you are pursuing a non-average life, you will quickly become unrelatable to your friends and partners unless you keep putting a dampener on your potential to avoid the thought of losing them in the pursuit of the highest version of yourself.

You don’t need to avoid socializing or dating, but if you don’t want to relate with 99% of people, and you probably don’t, get used to loving the time you have with yourself.

Do everything in your power to never get a job.

When I was around 15 years old, I had an intense burst of insight.

If I got a typical job like most people, I would end up like most people. A third of my time would disappear as soon as I accepted the offer. Another third of my time would be spent asleep. And the last third would be spent doing nothing worthwhile, because work you hate – no matter how simple – is the most draining thing in the world.

For the people who have read this far and agreed with most things I’ve said, I know what type of person you are, and this next statement won’t be a shocker to you:

You need to start a business.

Immediately.

You’re not the person who’s going to furiously type out how “not everyone should start a business” in the comments.

You are the person who wants control over your time, energy, and money. You understand that the good life stems from an increasing level of challenge, as that’s how you develop yourself, and that in 99% of jobs, the level of challenge comes to a halt 1-2 years in. It psychologically castrates you.

It really doesn’t matter what kind of business you start because what you do 2-3 years from now will be completely different.

You won’t get it right the first time.

So keep it simple at the start.

Do something low-cost, beginner level, and popular (because saturation is a sign that people need it, and 95% of people suck at it, so if you have a shred of ambition, you can make it work.)

This is the current beginner to advanced business meta with minimal risk involved:

Sell a service (freelancing or agency)

Build an audience while doing manual outreach

Launch an information product or community

Now you have a skillset and cash flow

Hire a team, or start a software or e-commerce business

Don’t worry about what skills to learn, because we’ll talk about that soon.

Set goals that f*cking scare you.

As I begin writing this section of the letter, my chest is getting tense and eyes are getting full, as I can’t help but hope that you all have a chance to feel what it’s like to reflect on your life and think, “I can’t believe how far I’ve come.”

Little Dan had dreams, but I never thought I’d actually write two books, build such a wide influence, be the CEO of a small yet growing startup, and live such a simple yet fulfilling life.

The pursuit of greatness can be shot down as materialistic in an instant by those who don’t understand.

But there’s something there.

Something deep.

A feeling so powerful that it can’t be replicated in any other way.

A source of energy so potent that big pharma’s strongest stimulant can’t compare.

A cosmic pull demanding you to become the highest version of yourself.

To replicate this, I want you to pull out a sheet of paper.

Title it “10 Goals, 10 Years.”

Write down 10 goals that make you feel uncomfortable.

Spread them out over the course of 10 years.

Focus solely on one massive goal per year.

Why?

Your mind expands to fill the goals set for achievement.

Building a $1 million company and a $100 million company requires the same amount of effort, but with different actions.

One could even argue that the owner of a local coffee shop works significantly harder than the owner of some online business, yet makes significantly less. Lots of context missing here, but don’t miss the point.

It’s common sense by now that hard work doesn’t lead to much in isolation.

You need to identify the actions that lead to the most outsized results, and if you don’t have large enough goals, you can’t identify large enough actions.

The greatest risk is no risk at all, and delusional goals change your brain.

I’ll save the explanation of that for another letter.

Make as much money as you can.

Money is tricky.

It’s such a large part of everyone’s lives that it has become intertwined with self-worth, morality, and survival, so people rarely see it for what it truly is.

Your parents tell you to save it.

Your pastor tells you to shun it.

Your culture tells you it’s not important.

So you don’t make it a priority, and a plethora of problems that can only be solved by money start to flood your life while you’re stuck making very little.

Very few people actually decide to see beyond the virtue signaling of others and form their own opinion, because in order to do so, they have to dedicate the time and brain power to getting rich. They would become the person they hate, even when they’ve never met that person. They’re living in a head filled with lies that influence their opportunity in the world.

Money is deeply ingrained into your mental, physical, spiritual, and obviously financial development. We don’t live in pre-industrial times. No, you can’t live like your ancestors, and I doubt you even want to, aside from the fact that you’re scared of money and refuse to accept your responsibility to make it.

“But Dan, what if I want to just make as much as I need?”

That’s perfectly fine, but again, you are limiting the level of challenge you can take on in multiple domains of your life. You can be mostly happy and satisfied, but I am talking specifically to those who cannot stand the thought of hitting a point in life where you repeat the same 6 months over and over again.

As dangerous and evil as money can be, you can’t build rockets or feed the world without it. Money is a globally accepted form of value, and very few people would work in such a motivated fashion without it. It’s an incredible construct. And whatever greater problems and innovations spring up throughout the course of evolution will probably require some kind of money, be it paper dollars or whatever currency that represents the exchange of value emerges.

The fact is, making money is a skill that can be developed like any other.

You aren’t good at making it because your identity is so latched onto unrealistic ideologies that skew your perception of everything related to money.

It’s pretty damn clear how you learn an instrument or get good at a video game.

You pick up the instrument. You learn the fundamentals. You attempt to play a song. You suck at it. Your brain starts to develop the pathways that lead to you playing the song. You choose a harder song. You suck again. You repeat the process.

With instruments and video games, there’s no risk.

It doesn’t matter if you fail.

But if you fail at making money, you can’t stop worrying about what everyone will think of you, how you wasted your time, how superficial you’re being, and whether it’s ever going to replace your current source of income.

Most people go about skill acquisition the completely wrong way.

It’s not about studying every source of information you can get your hands on.

It’s about actually playing the fucking game and improving based on what you did wrong the last time.

When you play a guitar, you choose a song you want to learn to play.

You try to play it, you fail, and then you learn a little technique that was used in that song. Once you learn that technique, then another, then another, you can now play many songs without needing to study anything.

If you want to make more money, then play a game that results in money until you win.

Self-actualize.

If the overarching aim that encompasses all other aims for your life is not to self-actualize, then it is to self-sabotage.

Every single action you take must align with the purpose of self-actualization.

If they don’t, then I would assume that you don’t have a deep reason behind why you do what you do.

It is difficult to explain the gravity of this.

Most people do not think about the life their actions will lead to.

They have a myopic focus on short-term pleasure that slowly beats them into a pulp without them realizing it until decades down the road. That is the worst possible place you could imagine yourself. Health issues that caught up with you. A mind that can’t adapt to the changing technological landscape. The actions you took were never a fully conscious choice, so they never led to anything great.

I shouldn’t have to show you the decades of psychological research that have amply dissected human needs and development. I shouldn’t have to explain that if you don’t self-actualize, you will drown in unnecessary pain.

For your own good, you need to train your mind to zoom out.

To adopt the perspective of the highest version of yourself and consult with them in real time.

It needs to become more than second nature to consider these 2 things before any small or large decision:

Who do I want to become?

Who do I not want to become?

Then, allow your decisions to be shaped by them both.

You don’t need to be perfect, but realize that most people never make a conscious decision in their lives.

If you can make the right choice even 30% of the time, those actions will be the ones that radically shape your future for the better.

Thank you for reading.

I hope it didn’t make too many people mad.

– Dan

articles.chinese:
【文章标题】20至30岁是“新手教程”阶段，千万别搞砸了  
【这是第1/5部分】

这封信会惹恼一些人，因为它只写给特定类型的人。

对大多数人而言，我听起来可能像个冷漠又讨人厌的混蛋——但唯有如此，才能让你们真正意识到当前处境的严重性。

话虽如此，请从现在起暂时关闭对细微差别的考量。

那些因本文直白到近乎残酷的坦率而勃然大怒的人，往往正过着相当糟糕的生活；他们在人格成长上，基本停滞于二十出头、二十五岁之前。

他们从未领悟到这一点：

要想最大限度地利用好自己的二十多岁，最好的办法，就是主动把它过得“最糟”。

你看，你只有两种选择：

——用你的二十多岁，去成为本该成为的那个自己；  
——或者，把人生中相同的六个月，重复过上一辈子。

倘若你在二十多岁时未能几乎穷尽自身潜力，只需环顾周遭社会，便不难发现：你终将变得和所有人一样。

你会陷入焦虑、不堪重负的循环之中，徒劳地试图重温生命中最后一次巅峰体验。你去同样的酒吧和电音派对，玩同样的电子游戏；你的人生巅峰体验之所以“巅峰”，只因你已足够年长，得以尝试新鲜事物，却尚未足够睿智，意识到那不过是人生所能抵达的最低微高峰——于是，你便用这些肤浅的活动填满余生。

多数人在23岁左右便进入发展平台期。

当你诚恳地问他们：“你这一生究竟在做什么？”他们往往无言以对，只能自信满满地回答：“就……过日子呗。”

问题在于，你根本意识不到原地踏步所带来的深远后果。

一旦真正看清，你就别无选择，只能改变。

多数人迈入三十岁之际，情感成熟度却仅相当于十五岁的少年。世界飞速向前奔涌，而你的思想、身体、精神乃至财务状况却纹丝不动。可这才是症结所在：所谓“维持现状”，不过是一种幻觉。若你不主动努力，便会不知不觉间，把自己一点点埋进平庸的泥沼——而且越陷越深，爬出来也愈发艰难。

你的二十多岁，只是“新手教程”，而非正式游戏本身；  
只是准备阶段，而非重头戏。

因此，以下有三大陷阱须竭力避开，以及三条路径助你彻底扭转局面。

若你能在二十多岁时为人生打好基础，即便青春不再，你的生活品质仍将持续提升。

切勿听信那些并未活成你理想模样的人。

真正活成你向往模样的人，极为稀少——  
仅占人口的1%；  
甚至可能更少。

其余99%的人，热衷于喋喋不休地指点你该如何生活，而他们自己早已挥霍掉了人生；他们一事无成，却偏要斩钉截铁地向你灌输：人生中最值得做的事，恰恰就是他们自己做过的事——而那些事，其实毫无价值可言。

他们会劝你“更现实一点”，劝你“降低目标”，劝你“活成他们的样子”，劝你“好好享受二十多岁！”——快去上班吧！做预算吧！把你那点可怜的积蓄拿去投资吧！然后日复一日、机械枯燥地做着自己憎恶的工作，直到五十岁，仿佛这是一场扭曲的成人礼。许多人嘴上说“希望你过得最好”，实则内心恐惧的是：不愿在你面前感到自惭形秽。

【文章标题】20—30岁是人生的关键学习期，千万别搞砸了  
【这是第2/5部分】

那些过着你向往生活的人，往往很低调。  
他们很难被发现。  
你要留心寻找这样的人。

对大多数人而言，把父母、老师或同龄人的建议奉为圭臬，无异于自取灭亡。  
尽快尝遍各种诱惑的滋味。

多数人把青春当成可随意挥霍的“货币”，而非用于投资的“本金”。  
他们纵情派对，他们吸烟——这些行为本身未必就是世界末日，但它们却会蚕食掉青春最宝贵的馈赠：时间、精力与专注力。

我上大学时也曾是个懵懂无知的年轻人，但我始终有一件事情在做，一件终将“买回我自由”的事。  

我并不是要你彻底杜绝上述所有行为。事实上，你反而应该尽快体验一番，以便清醒地意识到它们不过是错误的选择。我真正想告诉你的，是必须确立一个足以重塑人生的远大目标——它要求你拿出最好的状态，从而让你真切感受到自身堕落所带来的负面影响。

普通人之所以意识不到酗酒和吸烟的问题，是因为他们的生活根本不要求高水平的表现：他们干着自己并不喜欢的案头工作，因此宿醉带来的萎靡与懒散，似乎也无关紧要。

然而，这些绝非仅有的社交干扰源。

我理解，你正值青春年少，渴望探索世界；我也明白，从出生起便受避孕药与环境毒素影响，你的荷尔蒙早已紊乱失衡。但请听清楚：当你正处于自我最糟糕的状态时，你绝不可能遇见此生挚爱。

倘若你志在追求一种不平凡的人生，那么除非你刻意压抑自己的潜力、以免在追寻“最卓越自我”的路上失去朋友或伴侣，否则你很快就会变得令身边人难以理解、无法共鸣。

你无需回避社交或恋爱，但如果你不想与99%的人产生共鸣——而你大概率的确不想——那就请习惯并珍视独处的时光。

竭尽所能，永远别去上班。

大约15岁时，我曾有过一次极为强烈的顿悟：  
倘若我像大多数人一样找一份普通工作，最终也只会沦为芸芸众生中的一员。一旦接受录用，我三分之一的时间便已悄然消失；再有三分之一将在睡眠中流逝；而剩下的三分之一，则注定一事无成——因为无论工作多么简单，只要你内心憎恶它，它便是世上最令人精疲力竭的事。

对于读到这里、且认同我前述大部分观点的读者，我深知你们是怎样的人；因此，接下来这句话，想必不会令你们感到意外：

你必须立刻创业。  

马上开始。  

你不是那种会急不可耐地在评论区敲下“并非人人都该创业”之类话的人。  
你是那个渴望掌控自己时间、精力与金钱的人；你深知，美好人生源于持续升级的挑战——唯有如此，人才能不断成长；你也清楚，在99%的工作岗位上，挑战的强度往往入职一两年后便戛然而止，而这，无异于在心理层面阉割了你。

【文章标题】20—30岁是“入门训练期”，千万别搞砸了  
【这是第3/5部分】

你最初创办什么类型的企业，其实并不重要——因为两三年后，你所从事的事业将彻底不同。  

你第一次尝试绝不可能就做对。  

所以起步阶段务必保持简单。  

选一件低成本、入门门槛低、且广受欢迎的事来做（因为市场饱和恰恰说明人们有真实需求；而95%的人做得极差，因此只要你有一丁点雄心，就能把它做成）。  

以下是当前风险最低、从新手进阶到高手的主流路径：  

提供一项服务（自由职业或成立小型代理机构）  
在手动开展客户拓展的同时，逐步积累自有受众  
随后推出一款信息类产品或一个付费社群  

此时，你已掌握核心技能，并建立起稳定现金流  

接着，便可组建团队，或转向软件开发、电商等更规模化业务  

别担心该学哪些技能——我们很快就会详谈。  

设定那些真正让你“心头一紧”的目标。  

当我开始撰写本节内容时，胸口不由发紧，眼眶也渐渐湿润——因为我忍不住期盼：愿你们每个人，终有一日能静下心来回望人生，由衷感叹：“真不敢相信，自己竟已走了这么远。”  

小时候的丹尼尔怀揣梦想，但我从未想过，自己真能写出两本书、建立起如此广泛的影响、成为一家虽小却稳步成长的初创公司CEO，过上一种既朴素又丰盈的生活。  

追求卓越，常被不理解的人瞬间斥为“物质主义”。  

但其中确有某种东西。  

某种深沉的东西。  

一种强大到无法以任何其他方式复制的感受。  

一种能量之源，其强度连制药巨头最强效的兴奋剂都望尘莫及。  

一种宇宙级的召唤，敦促你蜕变为最卓越的自己。  

为重现这种状态，请你立刻拿出一张白纸。  

在顶端写下标题：“十年十项目标”。  

列出十个令你感到不适的目标。  

将它们均匀铺排在十年时间里。  

每年只聚焦于一个宏大的目标。  

为什么？  

因为你的思维会自然延展，去匹配你为自己设定的成就标尺。  

打造一家年营收百万美元的公司，与打造一家年营收亿美元的公司，所需付出的努力总量或许相差无几，但具体行动却截然不同。  

甚至有人会说：一家街角咖啡馆老板的辛劳程度，远超某家线上生意的创始人，可收入却少得多。此处省略诸多背景细节，但请勿忽略核心要义。  

如今已是常识：单靠埋头苦干，若脱离方向与策略，几乎难有建树。  

你必须识别出那些能带来最大杠杆效应的关键行动；而若目标本身不够宏大，你就永远无法发现足够宏大的行动。  

最大的风险，恰恰是“零风险”；而看似狂妄的目标，真的会重塑你的大脑。  

这一机制的详细解释，我留待下一封信再展开。  

尽可能多地赚钱。  

金钱很微妙。  

它在每个人生活中占据如此重要的位置，以至于早已与自我价值、道德判断乃至生存本能纠缠不清，以致人们极少能看清它的本来面目。  

父母告诫你要存钱；  
牧师劝你远离金钱；  
你的文化告诉你：金钱并不重要。

【文章标题】20—30岁是学习阶段，千万别搞砸了  
【这是第4/5部分】

于是你便不把它当作优先事项，而一大堆唯有金钱才能解决的问题却开始汹涌而至，可你却卡在收入微薄的困境中难以脱身。

真正愿意穿透他人“道德表演”的表象、独立形成自己见解的人少之又少——因为要做到这一点，你就必须投入时间与脑力去致富。你甚至会因此变成自己所憎恶的那种人，尽管你从未真正见过那样的人。你活在一个满是谎言的头脑里，而这些谎言正悄然侵蚀着你在现实世界中的机遇。

金钱已深深嵌入你的心理、生理、精神乃至显而易见的财务发展之中。我们早已不是前工业时代的人了。不，你无法像祖先那样生活；而且我怀疑，除了因恐惧金钱、拒绝承担创富责任之外，你其实根本不想那样生活。

“但丹，如果我只想挣到够用的钱呢？”

这当然完全没问题。但再次强调，你是在主动限制自己在人生多个领域所能迎接的挑战高度。你或许能获得大体上的幸福与满足，而我此刻所特别想对话的，是那些一想到人生某天会陷入“每六个月重复一次”的循环就无法忍受的人。

诚然，金钱可能既危险又邪恶，但没有它，你既造不出火箭，也养不活全世界。金钱是一种全球通行的价值载体，若没有它，极少有人能保持如此强烈的内在驱动力去工作。它本身就是一个非凡的社会建构。而无论人类演化进程中涌现出怎样更宏大的问题与创新，它们很可能都需要某种形式的货币——无论是纸币美元，还是未来任何一种用以衡量和交换价值的新通货。

事实就是：赚钱是一项技能，和其他任何技能一样，可以通过训练习得。

你之所以不擅长赚钱，并非能力不足，而是你的自我认同被种种脱离现实的意识形态牢牢捆绑，从而扭曲了你对一切与金钱相关事物的认知。

你如何学会一门乐器，或如何在电子游戏中变得高手，道理再清楚不过了：

你拿起乐器；学习基本功；尝试演奏一首曲子；结果弹得糟糕透顶；大脑随之逐步构建起通往熟练演奏这首曲子的神经通路；接着你选择一首更难的曲子；再次弹得一团糟；然后不断重复这一过程。

学乐器、打游戏，毫无风险可言——失败了也无所谓。

但若你在赚钱这件事上失败了，你就无法停止担忧：别人会怎么看你？你是否白白浪费了时间？自己是不是太肤浅？这笔收入究竟何时才能取代你现有的谋生来源？

大多数人习得技能的方式，从一开始就是错的。

它并非意味着要穷尽一切你能接触到的信息源去研读学习；  
而是要真正投身其中，亲自“下场玩”，并根据上一次做错的地方，持续调整、精进。

当你弹吉他时，你会挑一首自己想学会的歌。

【文章标题】20至30岁是人生的关键学习期，切莫荒废  

【这是第5/5部分】  

你试着演奏一首歌，失败了；接着，你从中学会了一种演奏技巧。掌握这一技巧后，再学下一个、再下一个……最终，你无需刻意研习，便能自如演奏大量曲目。  

若想赚更多钱，那就专注投入一项能带来收入的游戏，直到赢为止。  

实现自我。  

倘若统摄你人生一切目标的终极目标，并非“实现自我”，那它就只能是“自我破坏”。  

你所做的每一件事，都必须与“实现自我”这一根本目的保持一致。  

倘若做不到这一点，我只能推断：你对自己所作所为的深层动因，其实一无所知。  

这种认知的分量，实在难以言表。  

大多数人从不思考——自己当下的行为，终将把人生引向何方。  
他们目光短浅，只盯着眼前的短暂欢愉；而这种欢愉日复一日地蚕食着他们，直至数十年后才猛然惊觉——那时，健康问题早已找上门来；心智已无法适应飞速变迁的技术环境；所有过往行动，从未经过真正清醒自主的选择，因此也从未导向任何值得称道的成就。  

我不必向你一一罗列数十年来心理学界对人类需求与发展所作的详尽研究；也不必再解释：倘若你无法实现自我，终将沉溺于本可避免的痛苦之中。  

为了你自己好，请务必训练大脑学会“拉远镜头”，退后一步审视全局。  
请主动代入那个最卓越、最理想的“未来的你”的视角，并在当下实时向他请教。  

在做任何大小决策之前，将以下两点内化为本能反应——甚至超越本能：  
我想成为怎样的人？  
我绝不想成为怎样的人？  
然后，让这两重答案共同塑造你的每一个决定。  

你无需完美无缺；但请明白：绝大多数人终其一生，从未做过一次真正清醒自主的选择。  
哪怕你仅能在30%的时间里做出正确选择，这些选择也将从根本上重塑你的未来，使之朝更美好的方向跃进。  

感谢阅读。  
希望这篇文章没有惹恼太多人。  
——丹

articles.title: How To Think Like A Genius (The Map Of All Knowledge)
articles.description: 教你如何进阶为二层思考者。
articles.english:
The mark of a free individual is that they get what they want in life.

This requires them to learn how to learn, how to earn, and how to think.

The last one – how to think – is the most important because your thoughts influence what you learn, how you act, and whether or not you can create a strategy that allows you to achieve the big goals that most people wouldn’t even think to achieve.

But here’s the thing: you don’t need to be smart to think like a genius.

In fact, you don’t want to be like most smart people. Smart people often aren’t that smart. They memorize facts to get a secure and high-paying job while overanalyzing the risk of doing what they want. Dumb people often run laps around smart people because they take the stupid risks that shift the trajectory of their lives.

Genius-level thinking isn’t about book smarts.

It’s about clarity.

That’s why most people end up in a life they hate and aren’t able to think of a way out. Their mind can’t sift through the overwhelm, anxiety, and stress so it continues to beat them down until they give up completely.

The good news is, thinking is a skill, and skills can be practiced.

I’ve always admired the articulation of Jordan Peterson, the magic behind Alan Watts, and the clarity of Daniel Schmachtenberger. I want to share with you one of the most powerful models that has yet to be conceived. It’s a synthesis of all of the world’s great philosophies, scientific discoveries, and psychological patterns that, if you spend enough time with it, will radically transform your life.

It doesn’t matter if you’re trying to figure out what you want to do with your life, become a spiritually enlightened monk, or build a billion-dollar company, this model will drastically shorten how quickly you can achieve those things.

This Map Of All Knowledge Is Mind-Blowing

“I don’t have to agree with everything you say, but I should attempt at least to understand it, for the opposite of mutual understanding is, quite simply, war.”

– Ken Wilber

This may sound obvious, but you have to think to solve a problem or achieve a goal.

You need to identify a problem.

You need to understand it deeply.

You need to hypothesize a reasonable goal.

You need to create and execute a strategy to achieve the goal.

Sounds simple, but it’s incredibly complex. Most businesses fail because they don’t build a product that actually solves a problem. Most relationships fail because problems are never identified. Most people fail in general because they simply can’t see a way out of their situation.

So, if you can improve your thinking, you can solve those problems or achieve those goals faster. When you map that out over a 10-year timeline, it’s not difficult to see that you can achieve 10x more than most people do in their entire lifetime.

Let me introduce you to the AQAL model from Ken Wilber, an American Philosopher who made it his life’s work to synthesize all knowledge and experience into one comprehensive theory of everything.

While Wilber has stated that his model is not the end-all be-all, I can confidently say that this model is one of those “hidden gems” that most people don’t care about for the simple reason that they can’t see beyond their own worldview.

AQAL stands for All Quadrants, All Levels.

Wilber found, through decades of study and 3 year sabbaticals, that all knowledge and experience mapped into four interconnected quadrants:

Individual Interior (Upper Left): Your personal thoughts, emotions, beliefs, and consciousness

Individual Exterior (Upper Right): Your behaviors, actions, and physical brain states

Collective Interior (Lower Left): Shared culture, values, and group consciousness

Collective Exterior (Lower Right): Systems, structures, and social institutions

For becoming a genius-level thinker, the utility of this model is that when you are facing any form of challenge, you can systematically examine it from all four quadrants or perspectives.

More importantly, most people only think from one quadrant and preach that as the “one true way.” Capitalists focus on the economic system, lower right. Scientific materialists focus on matter and behavior, upper right. Religions focus on shared faith, lower left. Stoics and Buddhists focus on the internal world, upper left.

The fact of the matter is that all of these perspectives are valid and overlapping. Locking yourself into one dogmatic worldview puts you in a box. Certain problems are best solved from certain perspectives, and if you can’t access the right one, you will experience unnecessary pain in life.

To make this clear, let’s run through a difficult example.

I think it’s safe to say that most people struggle to figure out what they want in life. That’s a hard problem that 90% of people get stuck on.

If you’ve heard of the Japanese concept of IKIGAI, think of the AQAL model like that, but on steroids, especially in this context.

Now, thinking is a conversation with yourself.

Idiotic thinking is a conversation that turns into an argument and ends fast because you latch onto one answer.

Genius thinking is a conversation that accurately covers multiple perspectives and synthesizes their best parts into a clear solution.

To begin figuring out what we want out of life, we ask a series of questions within each quadrant in the map of all knowledge and experience.

Here are some examples I came up with (Note that this takes time. True thinking is difficult).

It may be wise to pull out a pen and paper.

Individual Interior (Upper Left) – Your Inner World

What are my core values and what truly matters to me?

What activities make me feel most alive and energized?

What fears or limiting beliefs are holding me back?

What does my intuition tell me when I quiet the mental noise?

Individual Exterior (Upper Right) – Your Actions & Capabilities

What are my natural talents and developed skills?

What does my behavior reveal about my true preferences?

What were some of my favorite things as a child?

What concrete steps am I taking and what life is that leading to?

Collective Interior (Lower Left) – Cultural & Social Context

What do my parents or religious leaders expect of me in terms of their idea of success?

How do my friends influence my career aspirations and life path?

How does the language I speak and digital culture I am exposed to influence my opportunities?

What shared values am I drawn to? What do I find meaningful?

Collective Exterior (Lower Right) – Systems & Structures

What are the current opportunities for jobs, careers, or entrepreneurship in today’s world?

How does the education system or internet shape my path?

What technological or social trends are creating new opportunities?

What systemic barriers or advantages do I face?

By using this model, you turn the question of “what do I do with my life?” into a comprehensive map that reveals how your authentic self, actual capabilities, personal calling, economic realities, and cultural contexts all interplay.

Rather than ending up with the answer of “I don’t know” or “I’m not interested in anything,” you may end up with a few realizations.

You might discover you value creativity over financial security.

You might discover that the fear of disappointing your parents is hindering your authentic desires.

You might notice that you procrastinate on certain tasks (to remove from your life or delegate) while you can’t stop talking about other interesting tasks.

You might realize that technology allows you to learn more, do more, and create a career path that wasn’t available in the recent past.

Those are deep, life-changing realizations that you may not have come to on your own.

And while that’s powerful, that’s only the first half of this model.

Why Smart People Are Incredibly Dumb

You could say that what humans selected for are genetics selected for memetics—our genetics selected for radical neuroplasticity and the capacity to have much more significant software upgrades that could change our capacity without needing hardware upgrades.

– Daniel Schmachtenberger

When I first came across this, I was blown away.

It made so much sense that it felt like my mind had expanded into a new dimension of thinking.

We covered the “All Quadrants” portion of AQAL, but not the “All Levels” portion.

All Levels refer to the developmental stages of consciousness that individuals and collectives can evolve through.

When it comes to thinking like a genius, this is crucial because most life conflicts or “impossible” problems exist because people are operating from different levels.

We’ve discussed this in depth before when discussing Spiral Dynamics and the 9 Stages of Ego development, so I want to focus on the 4 key levels that will change how you think about the world.

These levels of development illustrate the dominant value systems of a person or culture. In other words, these levels show what people, cultures, or systems hold as central and important, which influence the decisions that are made and how problems are perceived and solved. Most people reside in the first three, while very few – let’s call them geniuses for the sake of this letter – fall into the fourth.

1) Premodern

These individuals, cultures, or systems follow established authority and traditions. Their thinking is black and white. There is only “one right way,” and that usually involves obeying a God or conforming to what is right and true.

2) Modern

They value science, individual achievement, and competition. You can best identify this level in universities, corporate structures, and self-help teachings. People with a modern worldview are dogmatic about the fact that success should be based on merit and results.

3) Postmodern

Postmodernists value relativistic thinking. Everyone’s truth is valid. Include everyone and ensure they are equal.

With each of these stages, there are good and bad parts, and in today’s world, postmodern thinking has gone pathological, resulting in things like DEI, gender politics, and attempting to dismantle all hierarchies, which is stupid and impossible.

The critical piece of these first 3 stages is that they cannot hold multiple perspectives. They are right and you are wrong. This makes it difficult for them to think outside of their stage, and even more difficult to solve personal and systemic problems that lead to beneficial progress for humanity.

This is why smart people are incredibly dumb.

4) Second-Tier

With enough effort and development, you can reach the stage of second-tier thinking.

At this stage, you are able to look backward and pull truths from all prior perspectives, opening up a world of complexity, systems thinking, and awareness.

It’s less about a black and white “I’m right and you’re wrong” and more about a nuanced “the best solution comes from a synthesis of all.” Authority is important, merit is important, equality is important, but many people can hold those contradictions in their minds long enough for them to be reconciled.

Genius thinkers understand that these are stages, not static identities you have for the rest of your life. They often act as “translators” between different stages.

If the problem is business related, they can put on the cap of a CEO and resolve it faster than someone who permanently wears the cap of a bible-thumper for clear reasons.

If the problem is in a personal relationship, mansplaining about female psychology may help, but it isn’t the best substitute for empathy, depending on the context.

If the problem is writing on social media to attract and help an audience of self-helpers, you must understand their psychology and the best way to navigate their mind to reach the next level of development.

When it comes to figuring out what you want in life, accepting that you are in a modern stage of development can allow you to zoom out a layer, notice your shortcomings, and account for them when acting toward a better life.

This is a dense topic.

We could continue talking about it for hours upon hours.

My challenge to you is to pursue this knowledge in your own time, by your own curiosity, because it will only enhance your ability to take control of your life.

Thank you for reading.

– Dan

articles.chinese:
【文章标题】如何像天才一样思考（全知识地图）  
【这是第 1/5 部分】

自由个体的标志，就在于他能获得自己真正想要的人生。

而要做到这一点，他必须学会三件事：如何学习、如何谋生，以及——如何思考。

其中最后一点——“如何思考”——最为关键，因为你的思想直接影响你学什么、如何行动，也决定你能否制定出一套行之有效的策略，从而实现那些绝大多数人甚至想都不敢想的宏大目标。

但这里有个关键点：你并不需要天生聪明，才能像天才那样思考。

事实上，你根本不想成为大多数“聪明人”那样的人。所谓“聪明人”，往往并不真有多聪明：他们死记硬背各种事实，只为求得一份安稳高薪的工作；同时又过度权衡风险，迟迟不敢去做自己真正想做的事。反倒是那些被贴上“愚笨”标签的人，常常把“聪明人”远远甩在身后——正因为他们敢于冒看似愚蠢的风险，从而彻底扭转了自己人生的轨迹。

天才级的思维，与书本上的聪明才智毫无关系。

它关乎的是清晰。

正因如此，多数人才最终陷入自己憎恶的人生，却苦思不得其解，找不到出路。他们的头脑无法从纷繁的过载信息、焦虑与压力中抽身而出，只能任其持续碾压，直至彻底放弃。

好消息是：思考是一种技能，而所有技能都可以通过练习来提升。

我始终钦佩乔丹·彼得森（Jordan Peterson）精准有力的表达，着迷于艾伦·瓦茨（Alan Watts）话语背后那种摄人心魄的智慧，也深深折服于丹尼尔·施马滕贝格（Daniel Schmachtenberger）所展现的非凡清晰度。现在，我想与你分享一个迄今尚未被世人构想出来的、极具力量的思想模型。它融汇了人类历史上所有伟大的哲学体系、科学发现与心理规律；只要你投入足够的时间去理解它、运用它，你的生命将发生翻天覆地的转变。

无论你正苦苦思索人生方向，还是立志成为一位精神开悟的僧人，抑或梦想打造一家市值百亿的公司——这个模型都将极大缩短你达成目标所需的时间。

这张《全知识地图》令人震撼

“我不必赞同你说的每一句话，但我至少应努力去理解它；因为相互理解的反面，说白了，就是战争。”

——肯·威尔伯（Ken Wilber）

这听起来或许显而易见：要解决问题或实现目标，你必须思考。

你需要识别出问题所在；  
你需要深入理解这个问题；  
你需要提出一个合理可行的目标；  
你需要设计并执行一套切实有效的策略，以达成该目标。

听起来简单，实则极其复杂。大多数企业之所以失败，是因为它们开发的产品根本没能真正解决任何实际问题；大多数关系之所以破裂，是因为双方从未真正识别出彼此之间存在的问题；而大多数人之所以普遍失败，归根结底，只是因为他们根本看不到自己处境之外的任何出路。

因此，只要你提升了思考能力，就能更快地解决问题、更高效地实现目标。若将这种提升放在十年的时间维度上加以审视，便不难发现：你所能达成的成就，很可能会是常人终其一生都难以企及的十倍之多。

【文章标题】如何像天才一样思考（全知识地图）  
【这是第2/5部分】

让我向您介绍美国哲学家肯·威尔伯提出的AQAL模型。威尔伯毕生致力于将人类全部知识与经验整合为一套包罗万象的“万物理论”。

尽管威尔伯本人强调，他的模型并非终极真理，但我可以肯定地说，这一模型堪称一颗“深藏不露的瑰宝”——大多数人之所以对其漠不关心，仅仅是因为他们无法超越自身固有的世界观。

AQAL是“All Quadrants, All Levels”（所有象限、所有层次）的缩写。

经过数十年潜心研究及三次为期三年的学术休假，威尔伯发现：人类一切知识与经验均可映射至四个相互关联的象限之中：

个体内在（左上象限）：你个人的思想、情绪、信念与意识状态  
个体外在（右上象限）：你的行为、行动以及大脑的生理状态  
集体内在（左下象限）：共享的文化、价值观与群体意识  
集体外在（右下象限）：各类系统、结构与社会制度  

对于培养天才级的思维能力而言，该模型的核心价值在于：当你面对任何挑战时，都能系统性地从这四个象限（即四种视角）逐一审视问题。

更重要的是，绝大多数人仅习惯于从单一象限出发思考，并将其奉为“唯一正解”：资本家聚焦于经济体系（右下象限）；科学唯物主义者专注于物质与行为（右上象限）；宗教传统侧重于共同信仰（左下象限）；斯多葛学派与佛教徒则深耕内在世界（左上象限）。

事实是，所有这些视角均真实有效，且彼此交叠、互为补充。若固守某一种教条式的世界观，无异于将自己关进思想的牢笼。某些问题天然更适合从特定视角切入解决；倘若你无法调用恰当的视角，便难免在生活中承受本可避免的痛苦。

为使这一点更清晰明了，我们不妨以一个颇具挑战性的实例展开分析。

我们可以有把握地说：多数人都难以厘清自己真正想要的人生方向——这的确是一道难题，约九成的人终其一生都困于此处。

若您听说过日本的“生存意义”（Ikigai）概念，那么不妨将AQAL模型视作它的强化升级版，尤其在此类人生议题上更是如此。

思考，本质上是一场与自我的对话。

愚钝的思考，是一场迅速演变为争执的自我对话——你刚抓住一个答案，对话便戛然而止。

而天才式的思考，则是一场能准确涵盖多重视角、并从中萃取精华、最终凝练出清晰解决方案的深度对话。

要开始探寻我们真正渴望的人生图景，我们需依据“全知识与经验地图”，在每个象限内提出一系列关键问题。

以下是我构思的一些示例（请注意：真正的思考需要时间，它从来都不轻松）。

此时，拿出一支笔和一张纸，或许是个明智之举。

个体内在（左上象限）——你的内在世界  

我最核心的价值观是什么？什么对我而言真正重要？  
哪些活动能让我感到最鲜活、最有能量？  
有哪些恐惧或限制性信念正在阻碍我前行？  
当我平息内心的杂音、回归宁静时，直觉究竟在向我传递什么信息？

【文章标题】如何像天才一样思考（全知识地图）  
【这是第3/5部分】

个体外在（右上象限）——你的行动与能力  

我天生具备哪些才能？又掌握了哪些后天习得的技能？  
我的行为透露出我内心真正偏爱什么？  
童年时期，我最钟爱的事物有哪些？  
我正在采取哪些切实可行的步骤？这些行动正将我引向怎样的人生？  

集体内在（左下象限）——文化与社会背景  

我的父母或宗教领袖所理解的“成功”，对我提出了怎样的期待？  
我的朋友如何影响我的职业志向与人生道路？  
我所使用的语言，以及我所接触的数字文化，如何塑造了我的发展机会？  
我被哪些共同价值观所吸引？什么让我感到有意义？  

集体外在（右下象限）——系统与结构  

当今世界，就业、职业发展或创业存在哪些现实机遇？  
教育体系或互联网如何塑造了我的成长路径？  
哪些科技或社会趋势正在催生全新的可能性？  
我面临哪些系统性的障碍或优势？  

借助这一模型，你便能将“我这辈子该做什么？”这一模糊提问，转化为一幅全景式地图——它清晰呈现了你真实的自我、实际的能力、内在的召唤、经济现实以及文化背景之间错综复杂的互动关系。  

你不再止步于“我不知道”或“我对什么都提不起兴趣”这类消极答案，反而可能获得若干深刻洞见：  

你或许会意识到，自己更珍视创造力，而非财务上的安稳；  
你或许会发现，害怕令父母失望的情绪，正悄然阻碍你追随内心真实渴望；  
你或许会注意到，面对某些任务时你总是拖延（意味着它们应从生活中剔除，或交由他人代劳），而对另一些饶有趣味的任务，你却滔滔不绝、欲罢不能；  
你或许会真切体会到，技术赋予了你前所未有的学习能力、行动力与创造空间——一条在不久之前尚不存在的职业路径，如今已向你敞开。  

这些洞见深邃而有力，足以重塑你的人生，而若单靠自己摸索，你很可能永远无法抵达。  

然而，这股力量虽强大，却仅是本模型的前半部分。  

为何聪明人往往愚不可及？  

正如丹尼尔·施马滕贝格所言：“人类进化所选择的，并非纯粹的基因，而是‘模因’（meme）——我们的基因恰恰选择了极致的神经可塑性，使我们得以实现远超硬件升级的‘软件升级’：即通过心智模式的跃迁，大幅提升自身能力，而无须等待生理结构的改变。”  

初次读到这段话时，我深受震撼。  
它如此合乎逻辑，以至于我仿佛感到自己的思维骤然拓展，跃入了一个崭新的认知维度。  

此前，我们已探讨了AQAL模型中的“所有象限”（All Quadrants）部分，却尚未触及“所有层级”（All Levels）部分。  
“所有层级”指的是个体与群体意识所能经历的发展阶段。  
而要像天才一样思考，这一维度至关重要——因为绝大多数人生冲突或看似“无解”的难题，其根源恰恰在于人们处于不同的意识发展阶段。

【文章标题】如何像天才一样思考（全知识地图）  
【这是第4/5部分】

我们此前在探讨螺旋动力学（Spiral Dynamics）及自我发展的九大阶段时，已对此作过深入讨论。因此，此处我将聚焦于四个关键层级——它们将彻底改变你看待世界的方式。

这些发展层级揭示了个人或文化所秉持的主导价值体系。换言之，它们展现了人们、文化或社会系统视作核心与重要之事，而这些观念又深刻影响着决策方式，以及人们对问题的感知与解决路径。多数人停留在前三个层级；极少数人——为便于行文，我们暂且称其为“天才”——则跃升至第四层级。

1）前现代层级  

此类个体、文化或系统遵从既定权威与传统。其思维非黑即白，只承认“唯一正确之道”，而这通常意味着服从神明，或顺应所谓“正当”与“真理”的规范。

2）现代层级  

该层级重视科学、个人成就与竞争精神。大学、企业组织架构及自助类读物，最能体现这一世界观。持有现代视角者坚信：成功必须以能力与实绩为依据，对此立场极为坚定。

3）后现代层级  

后现代主义者推崇相对主义思维：每个人所信奉的“真理”皆具有效性；必须包容所有人，并确保人人平等。

上述每个阶段均有其合理之处，亦有其局限所在。而在当今时代，后现代思维已走向病态化，催生出诸如多元、公平与包容（DEI）运动、性别政治，以及试图彻底瓦解一切等级结构等现象——这既愚蠢，亦不可行。

前三个阶段最关键的症结在于：它们无法同时容纳多种视角。“我正确，你错误”是其根本逻辑。这使得人们难以跳出自身所处的发展阶段进行思考，更遑论有效应对那些关乎个人成长与社会系统演进、并最终推动人类整体福祉的复杂难题。

正因如此，聪明人反而可能愚不可及。

4）第二层级  

只要付出足够努力并持续精进，你便有可能抵达“第二层级”思维。

在此层级上，你能够回溯过往各阶段，从中汲取真知灼见，从而开启一个充满复杂性、系统性思维与深层觉察的广阔世界。

这里不再执着于非此即彼的“我对你错”，而转向更为精微的洞见：“最优解，往往诞生于对所有视角的整合与升华。”权威值得尊重，能力理应嘉许，平等不可或缺——而真正成熟的心智，恰恰能长久地容纳这些看似矛盾的价值，在张力中促成内在的调和与统一。

天才型思考者深知：这些层级是动态演进的阶段，而非伴随终生、一成不变的身份标签。他们常扮演不同发展阶段之间的“翻译者”。

倘若问题关乎商业运营，他们可自如切换为首席执行官的思维模式，其解决效率远超那些始终戴着“圣经布道者”帽子、却缺乏现实适配性的个体——原因显而易见。

倘若问题发生在亲密关系之中，就女性心理大谈特谈的“男性说教”或许偶有裨益，但若脱离具体情境，它绝非共情所能替代的最佳方案。

【文章标题】像天才一样思考（全知识地图）  
【这是第 5/5 部分】

如果你面临的问题是：如何在社交媒体上写作，以吸引并帮助一群自助型读者，那么你必须深入理解他们的心理机制，并掌握最有效的方式，引导他们的思维迈向更高层次的发展。

当思考自己真正想要的人生时，若能坦然接纳自己正处于现代发展阶段这一事实，便能退后一步、拉开视角，清晰察觉自身的局限，并在追求更美好生活的行动中主动将这些局限纳入考量。

这是一个信息密度极高的主题。

我们甚至可以就此连续探讨数小时而不觉疲倦。

我向你提出的挑战是：请凭自己的好奇心，在属于你自己的时间里主动探索这一知识——因为唯有如此，你掌控自身人生的能力才会真正得到提升。

感谢阅读。  
——丹  

延伸阅读：自我发展的九大阶段：如何变得比99%的人更睿智

sentences.english: The mark of a free individual is that they get what they want in life.
sentences.chinese: 一个自由个体的标志，就是能获得自己真正想要的人生。

sentences.english: This requires them to learn how to learn, how to earn, and how to think.
sentences.chinese: 这要求他们学会如何学习、如何谋生，以及——如何思考。

sentences.english: Your thoughts influence what you learn, how you act, and whether or not you can create a strategy that allows you to achieve the big goals that most people wouldn’t even think to achieve.
sentences.chinese: 你的思想影响着你学什么、如何行动，以及能否制定出策略，去实现那些大多数人甚至不敢想象的宏大目标。

sentences.english: You don’t need to be smart to think like a genius.
sentences.chinese: 你不必聪明，也能像天才一样思考。

sentences.english: Genius-level thinking isn’t about book smarts. It’s about clarity.
sentences.chinese: 天才级思维无关书本知识，而在于清晰度。

sentences.english: Their mind can’t sift through the overwhelm, anxiety, and stress so it continues to beat them down until they give up completely.
sentences.chinese: 他们的头脑无法梳理纷杂的信息、焦虑与压力，于是持续被击垮，直至彻底放弃。

sentences.english: Thinking is a skill, and skills can be practiced.
sentences.chinese: 思考是一项技能，而技能是可以通过练习提升的。

sentences.english: It doesn’t matter if you’re trying to figure out what you want to do with your life, become a spiritually enlightened monk, or build a billion-dollar company — this model will drastically shorten how quickly you can achieve those things.
sentences.chinese: 无论你是在探索人生方向、追求精神开悟，还是打造十亿美元企业，这一模型都将极大缩短你达成目标所需的时间。

sentences.english: AQAL stands for All Quadrants, All Levels.
sentences.chinese: AQAL 代表‘所有象限、所有层级’。

sentences.english: All knowledge and experience mapped into four interconnected quadrants.
sentences.chinese: 所有知识与经验都可映射到四个相互关联的象限中。

sentences.english: Individual Interior (Upper Left): Your personal thoughts, emotions, beliefs, and consciousness.
sentences.chinese: 个体内在（左上）：你的个人思想、情绪、信念与意识。

sentences.english: Individual Exterior (Upper Right): Your behaviors, actions, and physical brain states.
sentences.chinese: 个体外在（右上）：你的行为、行动及大脑的生理状态。

sentences.english: Collective Interior (Lower Left): Shared culture, values, and group consciousness.
sentences.chinese: 集体内在（左下）：共享的文化、价值观与群体意识。

sentences.english: Collective Exterior (Lower Right): Systems, structures, and social institutions.
sentences.chinese: 集体外在（右下）：系统、结构与社会制度。

sentences.english: Most people only think from one quadrant and preach that as the 'one true way.'
sentences.chinese: 多数人只从一个象限出发思考，并将其奉为‘唯一真理’。

sentences.english: All of these perspectives are valid and overlapping.
sentences.chinese: 所有这些视角都是有效且彼此重叠的。

sentences.english: Locking yourself into one dogmatic worldview puts you in a box.
sentences.chinese: 将自己禁锢于一种教条式的世界观中，等于将自己关进牢笼。

sentences.english: Genius thinking is a conversation that accurately covers multiple perspectives and synthesizes their best parts into a clear solution.
sentences.chinese: 天才式思维是一场对话——它准确涵盖多个视角，并将其中最优部分综合成清晰的解决方案。

sentences.english: What are my core values and what truly matters to me?
sentences.chinese: 我的核心价值观是什么？什么对我而言真正重要？

sentences.english: What fears or limiting beliefs are holding me back?
sentences.chinese: 哪些恐惧或限制性信念正在阻碍我前进？

sentences.english: What does my behavior reveal about my true preferences?
sentences.chinese: 我的行为揭示了我真实的偏好是什么？

sentences.english: How do my friends influence my career aspirations and life path?
sentences.chinese: 我的朋友如何影响我的职业志向与人生道路？

sentences.english: What systemic barriers or advantages do I face?
sentences.chinese: 我面临哪些系统性的障碍或优势？

sentences.english: All Levels refer to the developmental stages of consciousness that individuals and collectives can evolve through.
sentences.chinese: ‘所有层级’指个体与集体可能经历的意识发展阶段。

sentences.english: Most life conflicts or 'impossible' problems exist because people are operating from different levels.
sentences.chinese: 大多数人生冲突或所谓‘无解’的问题，根源在于人们处于不同的意识层级。

sentences.english: At this stage, you are able to look backward and pull truths from all prior perspectives.
sentences.chinese: 在此阶段，你能回溯过往，从所有先前视角中汲取真理。

sentences.english: It’s less about a black and white 'I’m right and you’re wrong' and more about a nuanced 'the best solution comes from a synthesis of all.'
sentences.chinese: 重点不再是非黑即白的‘我对你错’，而是更精微的‘最优解源于对所有视角的综合’。

sentences.english: Genius thinkers understand that these are stages, not static identities you have for the rest of your life.
sentences.chinese: 天才型思考者明白：这些是发展中的阶段，而非你终生不变的固定身份。

sentences.english: They often act as 'translators' between different stages.
sentences.chinese: 他们常充当不同发展阶段之间的‘翻译者’。

sentences.english: Thinking is a conversation with yourself.
sentences.chinese: 思考，就是与自己的对话。

articles.title: The Death Of Thoughtful Creation (& How To Get Ahead Of Everyone Else)
articles.description: 在快节奏时代，如何通过专注创作保持竞争优势。
